An employee at the Green Mount Commons location declined to give his name, but said they learned of the closing Monday morning around 10 a.m. All signage was gone from each location by Tuesday afternoon. Multiple notices were posted on the doors and drive-thru speaker at Green Mount stating, ”This location is closed. Thank you for your business. Please visit our other location in Belleville.” The Hardee’s location at 1617 N. Belt West remains open. Other metro-east locations also remain open in O’Fallon, Caseyville, Collinsville, Glen Carbon, Granite City, and Waterloo.

articles.headline: Layne's Chicken Fingers Hits 50 Units And 24 New Franchise Deals In 2026
articles.summary: Fifty open restaurants. Two dozen new franchise agreements. A California debut in the works. Layne's Chicken Fingers didn't just have a good start to 2026 — it hit the growth inflection point that separates emerging concepts from real, scalable franchise brands. At the close of the second quarter, the Texas "Born and Breaded" chicken finger franchise has expanded to more than 50 operating restaurants and signed two dozen franchise agreements, fueled by a mix of internal development and fresh operators joining the system. The brand also landed a placement on the prestigious Franchise 500 — a credibility marker that matters when you're courting multi-unit operators and institutional capital.

articles.headline: Wingstop Added More Restaurants Than Any US Chain In 2025, Report Says
articles.author: Fernando Cervantes Jr.
articles.summary: Americans can't seem to get enough Wingstop. The Texas-based chicken chain opened more new restaurants than any other U.S. chain in 2025, adding 382 locations and beating out major brands including Chipotle, Starbucks, Chick-fil-A and Taco Bell, according to a new ranking from QSR Magazine. Wingstop's first-place ranking comes as the chicken chain continues its rapid expansion. According to QSR Magazine, Wingstop had 785 locations when it went public in 2015. By the end of fiscal 2025, the company operated 3,056 restaurants worldwide.

articles.headline: 11 Discontinued KFC Items That Deserve A Revival
articles.author: Amy Bell
articles.summary: While KFC remains a staple for its famous bone-in fried chicken, there are a lot of beloved menu items that have disappeared over the years. Some have been gone for decades, while others linger in our more recent memories. With enough customer interest and petitions, we've seen quite a few beloved but discontinued KFC menu items make a comeback. So, it seems that the company is listening to the voices of its customers. For example, we've seen potato wedges, popcorn chicken, Snackers, Twisters, and honey BBQ wings return to the menu. So, take heart if you've been wishing a favorite discontinued KFC menu item would make a return.

articles.headline: 5 Common Customer Complaints About KFC's Mashed Potatoes
articles.author: Deepak Narayanan
articles.summary: Let's start with the disclaimer that there is no single correct way to make mashed potatoes. Some people like it silky smooth, others like the textural variety that comes with a few lumps. Mashed potatoes can be hearty or decadent. They can be minimalist, loaded, or served with gravy. In fact, even the type of potato you pick has a bearing on the mash you end up with, not to mention all the different methods you can employ to make mashed potatoes. Basically, if you're running a professional kitchen, it should be hard to go wrong with mashed potatoes — which is why the sheer variety of complaints customers have about KFC's take on the global classic is noteworthy. Kentucky Fried Chicken has been serving mashed potatoes forever. Even an original 1952 menu that popped up on Reddit has whipped potatoes on it. KFC's love affair with mash continued into the 21st century. In 2006, KFC famously launched its Mashed Potato Bowls, which topped its mash with corn, fried chicken, and gravy. More recently, it introduced the Smash'd Potato Bowl, where the mash is topped with fries, bacon, and cheese.

articles.headline: Stop The Trucks: Inside Taco Bell’s Rush To Contain Cyclospora
articles.author: Heather Haddon
articles.summary: The word went out from Taco Bell’s leaders on the evening of July 14: Stop the trucks. Public-health officials that night had notified the chain that the shredded lettuce garnishing Crunchwrap Supremes, Cantina Chicken Burritos and other menu items was the suspected culprit in a rapidly expanding cyclospora outbreak. Executives rushed to halt shipments then on their way to hundreds of Taco Bell’s 7,785 U.S. locations.

articles.headline: Taco Bell Offering $1 Lettuce-Free Deal Amid Cyclospora Outbreak
articles.author: Greta Cross, Melina Khan
articles.summary: As the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak impacts its foot traffic, Taco Bell is offering a $1 lettuce-free menu item promotion. In a social media post made the afternoon of July 22, Taco Bell promoted $1 Enchiritos, a flour tortilla filled with ground beef, beans, diced onions, cheddar cheese and a red sauce. The temporary menu item does not include lettuce. The social media post did not explicitly say the deal was created because of the cyclosporiasis outbreak. "Okay, now please just keep the enchirito on permanent," one Instagram user commented on Taco Bell's post promoting the deal. The offer comes as the fast-food chain has experienced a nosedive in foot traffic since its lettuce was linked to the outbreak of cyclosporiasis, which causes diarrhea and other gastrointestinal issues, by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

articles.headline: Wendy's Best Chicken Item Isn't The One You'd Expect — You May Need To Change Up Your Order
articles.author: Sara Klimek
articles.summary: When you think of Wendy's, what comes to mind? For many, it's the iconic Frosty, the flavors of which one of our tasters tried and ranked, its chili, or its Baconator. However, one of the most slept-on categories at the iconic fast food chain is its chicken. When we sent a writer to rank every Wendy's chicken item, they were surprised by the item that took the top spot in their rankings. It wasn't the nuggets, nor was it some derivative of the chicken sandwich. Rather, it was the Cobb Salad, which features a lettuce base, grilled chicken, diced tomatoes, shredded cheddar, chopped hard-boiled eggs, applewood-smoked bacon, crispy fried onions, and a side of ranch dressing. Our taster appreciated how all of the elements of this salad balanced each other, with the bacon adding salt, cheese adding richness, and chicken adding heartiness. Although it might not be the item you instinctively order at the chain, which is more often associated with burgers and Frostys than salads, it's surely a chicken item that can hold its own.

articles.headline: Wendy’s Is Bringing An International Hit To US Menus
articles.author: Madison Troyer
articles.summary: Over the last few years, limited-time offers (or LTO’s) have become one of the restaurant industry’s most-used tools. Chains like McDonald’s, Taco Bell, Wendy’s, and Chick-fil-A have come to rely on them as a way to generate buzz, create urgency, and drive foot traffic. In fact, between 2020 and 2024, the number of LTO’s offered by restaurants increased by 53% according to data from Technomic that was shared with Axios. For their part, customers love the ever-fresh nature of these menu additions. “52% of consumers say that the availability of an appealing limited-time offer is important when they’re deciding which restaurant to visit,” Lizzy Freier, director of menu research & insights at Technomic, told Axios.

articles.headline: Say 'Queso': Why Chipotle Is My Go-To Restaurant Rewards Program
articles.author: Eric Rosen
articles.summary: I'm not what you would call a fast-food connoisseur. You won't find me tearing into mass-made burgers or footlong subs except, perhaps, while dashing through an airport on an all-too-short connection between flights. I do, however, regularly stop by my neighborhood Chipotle to pick up healthy fast-casual meals that fill me up without emptying my bank account. What I order depends on the day — sometimes I'm a carnitas burrito bowl kind of guy, while other days, I just want simple chicken tacos and a side of guacamole. Regardless of what I decide to order, I always make sure to log my purchase in the Chipotle Rewards app, one of the only loyalty program apps on my phone that's not all about airline miles or hotel points. Doing so ensures I earn points with each purchase that can then be redeemed for a free item later.

articles.headline: Burger King Makes Major Changes After Thousands Of Customers Sounded Off
articles.author: Teresa Mull
articles.summary: Visitors to Burger King may soon notice several changes inspired by updates that customers of the fast-food chain said they wanted. "Earlier this year, we opened our phone lines and invited people to share their honest feedback, and they did," a Burger King representative told Fox News Digital. "One of the biggest takeaways was that our guests want to feel welcomed when they walk in, know their order will be made the way they asked and have confidence that if something isn't right, we'll make it right." Burger King said the initiative generated thousands of customer phone calls and text messages. Four months later, the company is introducing two strategies aimed at improving customer service and order accuracy.

articles.headline: PAW Patrol Toys Arrive At Burger King Ahead Of New Movie
articles.summary: Burger King has launched a new King Jr. Kids’ Meal promotion tied to the upcoming release of PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie, which arrives in theaters August 14. Beginning Wednesday, King Jr. Kids’ Meals will include one of six toys featuring characters from the film. The collection includes Chase, Marshall, Rubble, Skye, Rex, and Rhubarb the T-Rex. Rex and Rhubarb are new characters appearing in the movie. The limited-time collection is part of Burger King’s broader effort to offer family-oriented experiences through its King Jr. Kids’ Meals.

articles.headline: FSR And QSR Launch First AI Workshop At Annual Conference
articles.summary: QSR AI Connect is designed around a simple belief: AI success isn't determined by the technology an organization purchases. Artificial intelligence is quickly becoming one of the most significant forces shaping the restaurant industry. From marketing and loyalty to operations, labor, guest experience, and enterprise decision-making, restaurant leaders are facing unprecedented opportunities to rethink how their businesses grow and operate. To help restaurant executives move beyond experimentation and develop a practical path forward, the QSR Evolution Conference, run by Arrowfly and the teams behind QSR and FSR magazines, is launching QSR AI Connect, a new executive initiative designed to help leaders navigate the rapidly evolving AI landscape through education, collaboration, and practical application.

articles.headline: How 62 Percent of AI Users Are Successfully Lowering Their Labor Costs
articles.author: Teresa Mull
articles.summary: Labor costs have not stopped rising for quick-service operators. But the industry’s outlook is beginning to shift. Restaurant365’s 2026 State of the Restaurant Industry Mid-Year Report found that 77 percent of operators experienced higher labor costs in the first half of 2026. The impact remains significant: 64 percent are operating below full capacity, 17 percent have limited operating hours, and 7 percent have closed on days they would normally be open. AI can also support a more disciplined labor strategy. The report found that 62 percent of operators using AI said it has reduced labor costs, while roughly one in three users reported overall cost reductions of 6 percent or more. For skeptical operators, Cohen recommends treating AI as a business analyst—not a replacement for people. It can help evaluate forecasts, employee availability, and sales data to build smarter schedules and reduce managers’ administrative workload.

articles.headline: The Next Generation Of QSRs Part 2: How AI, Personalization Are Turning Loyalty Into A Growth Engine
articles.author: Valerie Gritton
articles.summary: As QSR brands navigate a more value-conscious consumer, the path forward is becoming increasingly interconnected. Part 1 of our Next-Gen series examined how rising costs and changing spending habits are redefining value, In Part 3, The Next Generation of QSR series will examine how operators are investing in technology, automation and operational efficiencies to improve performance, support teams and build a stronger foundation for growth. In today's quick-service landscape, growth is no longer defined by how much consumers are willing to spend — it's how often they choose to show up. As traffic patterns soften and value perception becomes more fragile, QSR operators are shifting capital toward investments designed to defend frequency, rebuild loyalty, and justify price points that continue to climb. Whether those goals are established and met through the use of AI or enhanced loyalty programs, personalization is a key selling point for both brands and consumers.

articles.headline: Chick-Fil-A Alerts DC, Maryland And Other Customers To Data Breach
articles.author: Tracy Johnke
articles.summary: Chick-fil-A rewards program members in D.C., Maryland and eight other states are getting letters warning that hackers may have gained access to partial payment information and other personal data during an “automated attack” on its website and app last month. The notice also suggests that some customers had money stolen from their Chick-fil-A One accounts. The attackers used email addresses and passwords obtained from a third-party source to gain access, Chick-fil-A said. Its investigation of the June breach determined the hackers may have accessed information including names, gift card balances, phone numbers, addresses and the last four digits of customers’ credit card numbers, the company said.

articles.headline: California-Based Fast-Food Chain Is No. 1 In The US. Hint: It’s Not In-N-Out
articles.author: Angela Rodriguez
articles.summary: California is home to some of the nation’s most recognizable fast-food chains, from iconic burger joints to growing coffee shops and ice cream favorites. USA Today readers recently ranked the best fast-food restaurants in 2026 — and one California-based restaurant chain took first place. Here’s a hint: It’s not In-N-Out. “On any given day, tens of millions of Americans are treated to irresistibly delicious food that’s in their hands just a few minutes (or less!) after ordering,” USA Today said in the new ranking, published July 15. “It takes a tremendous amount of hard work and preparation to deliver that sort of speed, quality and scale.”

articles.headline: Birdcall Intends To Become The Next Chicken Success Story
articles.summary: Birdcall—an emerging 17-unit chicken chain out of Colorado—is quickly expanding. The fast casual plans to open almost 100 locations in six states over the next five years. The initial pipeline will primarily focus on Midwestern states, such as Indiana, Kansas, Missouri, Nebraska, Ohio, and Wisconsin. VP of franchise development Justin Livingston says it’s a matter of right concept, right place, and right time. He sees consumers becoming tighter with their spending. And if a brand earns their money, “it better be an amazing experience,” he adds. That means putting the customer first and considering the impact of staffing, ingredients, and community.

articles.headline: Layne's Chicken Fingers Celebrates 50 Restaurants; Rapid Q2 Growth
articles.summary: Layne's Chicken Fingers awarded two dozen new franchise deals in the first half of 2026, expanding its operating footprint to more than 50 restaurants through a blend of both internal and external development, according to a press release. The Texas-based franchise reached its 50-restaurant milestone during the second quarter. Driven by expanding existing operators and new franchisees joining the system, Layne's established a 12-unit deal in California with tenured IHOP operators and a 30-unit agreement in Oklahoma with existing franchisee Taylor Thomas. "We've added dozens of units to the pipeline this year, and we've also opened a significant number," CEO Garrett Reed said in the press release.

articles.headline: KFC Once Tried To Be More Than A Fried Chicken Chain
articles.author: Dave Spencer
articles.summary: Did you know that, for a brief moment in its history, KFC could have replaced that "FC" with "RB 'n' H"? That's because, fun fact, the iconic chicken chain once experimented with roast beef and ham. By 1967, according to retroist.com, Kentucky Fried Chicken (as it was called at the time) had become so popular that it was one of the country's ten largest restaurant chains. In fact, it was popular enough that the brand decided to try its hand at roast beef and ham. The new chain was called Kentucky Roast Beef 'n' Ham and even used Colonel Sanders' trademark 11 herbs and spices in preparing the meat, although I can't help but wonder how seasonings earmarked for chicken would work with beef and ham.

articles.headline: This Secret KFC Meal Is One Of The Best Deals On The Menu
articles.author: Molly Burford
articles.summary: Well, it looks as though Cracker Barrel may have a bit of competition for its fan-favorite country fried steak meal, as KFC is now offering its own rendition of the hearty comfort food classic for just $4.99. However, there is a tiny catch: it will only be available at select KFCs on Wednesdays. At participating KFC locations, fans can order the affordable $4.99 Country Fried Steak Meal, which features a generous helping of Southern comfort food with everything you’d expect: crispy, golden fried steak smothered in a hearty white gravy, served with a side of mashed potatoes covered in cream gravy, coleslaw, and a warm biscuit. Yum!

articles.headline: The Old-Fashioned Kentucky Diner That’s Been Dishing Up Legendary Chicken Dinners For Decades
articles.author: Mason Whitaker
articles.summary: Tucked along Shelbyville Road in Shelbyville, Kentucky, Claudia Sanders Dinner House is one of those rare places where history and home cooking meet on the same plate. Founded by Claudia Sanders, wife of the legendary Colonel Harland Sanders of KFC fame, this charming restaurant has been serving up Southern comfort food for decades. With a warm, old-fashioned atmosphere and a menu packed with crowd-pleasing classics, it draws visitors from near and far. Whether you’re a first-timer or a loyal regular, this beloved Kentucky gem never disappoints. Some restaurants are known for one dish so good it practically defines them, and at Claudia Sanders Dinner House, that dish is undeniably the fried chicken. Rooted in the same Kentucky tradition that made Colonel Sanders a household name, this chicken carries serious culinary history on every crispy piece.

articles.headline: Historic Scottsdale Taco Bell Gets Second Life As Filiberto's
articles.author: Jessica Boehm
articles.summary: The iconic old-school Taco Bell building in south Scottsdale, which served its final crunchwraps more than a year ago, is getting a new purpose. And dare we say it feels a little kismet? State of play: Local Mexican chain Filiberto's appears to be taking over the mission-style restaurant. It's been painted bright red and a sign announcing the new tenant hangs where Taco Bell's did for more than 50 years, 12 News reported. What they're saying: "Like the Roman Catholic Church taking over old Rome ruins," one fan posted on Instagram. Why it matters: The restaurant, which first opened in the 1960s, was the nation's 31st Taco Bell location and was among the oldest still operating in the U.S when it closed last April.

articles.headline: A New Restaurant Is Moving Into Scottsdale’s Vintage Taco Bell. What To Know
articles.author: Sara Crocker
articles.summary: Fans of architecture and fast Mexican fare, rejoice! After more than a year sitting vacant, the kitchen previously home to a vintage Taco Bell, will soon be alive with cooks preparing tacos, burritos and tostadas. Filiberto’s will open in the former Scottsdale Taco Bell on McDowell Road near Hayden Road in August, Luis Espinoza, the restaurant chain’s real estate broker, confirmed to Phoenix New Times. He anticipates the restaurant will open in mid-to-late August. “We’re excited,” he said, noting the Filiberto’s would keep the same “historic” look. The restaurant has a notable history as Taco Bell’s store No. 31, the last vintage cantina in Arizona and one of fewer than 10 nationwide that served architectural nostalgia with their Crunchwrap Supremes.

articles.headline: $1 Frostys Return To Wendy’s — Here’s How To Get The Sweet Treat All Summer
articles.author: Faran Krentcil
articles.summary: Wendy’s is freezing prices on a crave-worthy item — but only for a limited time. From now until August 23, the fast food hub is bringing back the $1 Frosty, helping budget-conscious snackers cool off from summer inflation with a dollop of the chain’s famous chocolate or vanilla frozen dessert. The $1 Frosty deal runs nationwide from July 20 through August 23, and it’s available in-restaurant, at the drive-thru, through the Wendy’s app and on Wendys.com. Want it delivered? Sorry — you’ll get frozen out of this deal. Likewise, if you’re trying to order in bulk, since the offer caps out at 10 sweet treats.

articles.headline: Chipotle Mexican Grill Nearing Completion Of New Lehigh Valley Location
articles.author: Ryan Kneller
articles.summary: A popular fast-casual restaurant chain known for its made-to-order tacos, burritos, quesadillas and other Mexican eats is expanding its footprint in the region. Chipotle Mexican Grill, with more than 4,100 locations worldwide, is planning to open a new location at 1900 Sullivan Trail in Forks Township. Construction on the Forks location has ramped up in recent months, and exterior signage was recently installed. An exact opening date has not yet been determined, but the Forks restaurant is scheduled to open “before the end of the year,” a Chipotle spokesperson told 69 News. In 2021, Bethlehem-based developer Posh Properties No. 46 Hanson LLC was granted conditional use approval to the construct the new Chipotle restaurant – with a drive-thru for pick-up orders – by the Forks Township Board of Supervisors.

articles.headline: What Is Burger King's 'Whopper Guarantee'? Do Other Fast-Food Chains Offer Similar Policies?
articles.author: Matt Cudahy
articles.summary: Burger King is offering a new promotion that might sound too good to be true. It's called the "Whopper Guarantee." According to the fast-food company's press release, if a Whopper, Burger King's flagship sandwich, does not meet a customer's expectations, they will not only receive a remade Whopper that meets their standards but also a coupon for a free future Whopper. "When Guests choose us, they expect high-quality food, orders made the way they asked, and a team that's there when they need us," said Tom Curtis, president of Burger King U.S. and Canada. "That's what these changes are about. We're raising the standard in our restaurants, so every Guest feels like they made the right choice."

articles.headline: Could AI-Powered QSR Technology Help Independents Compete With Larger Chains?
articles.summary: The quick service restaurant (QSR) industry is not the same as it once was, and businesses need to keep up if they want to remain competitive. Customer expectations are forever changing as people seek convenience at a reasonable price. This is hard for QSRs to live up to as the cost of living continues to increase, but new digital systems have opened up new doors. Artificial intelligence (AI) is a phrase that is all around us at the moment, and the QSR industry is no exception. More and more business owners are coming to realize that they, too can introduce new tools without breaking the bank. As shown by the graph below, the use of restaurant management software is growing year on year in the QSR industry, and this is expected to continue at a compound annual growth rate of over 19 percent between now and 2033. This tells us that AI is not just a fad, but the start of the new normal that all businesses are going to have to get up to speed with if they want to keep up with larger chain restaurants.

articles.headline: Converge AI Extends Its AI-Native Workspace To The Restaurant Industry
articles.summary: Converge AI today outlined how its AI-native workspace can support restaurant marketing, operations, and guest engagement, as the company advances follow-up conversations with industry leaders and multi-unit operators at CREATE 2026, the Nation’s Restaurant News foodservice conference at Terranea Resort. The restaurant industry is among the most operationally demanding sectors of the US economy. Multi-unit brands coordinate campaign calendars, limited-time offer rollouts, franchisee communications, guest feedback, and unit-level performance across dozens or hundreds of locations, often with lean corporate teams supporting field operations. Against this backdrop, industry conversation is shifting from whether AI can be applied in restaurants to where it can deliver measurable value in everyday operations. Converge AI is built for that shift. Rather than adding another standalone tool to an already crowded technology stack, the platform brings specialized AI products into a shared context layer, allowing work and business knowledge created in one part of the business or organization to carry into the next.

articles.headline: We Tried McDonald’s’ Sweet New Breakfast Sandwich
articles.author: Griffin Parker
articles.summary: McDonald’s doesn’t update their breakfast menu every day, so it’s worth paying attention when they do turn the innovation gaze away from lunch and dinner for once (even if we are excited about that new Caesar sauce). Much like the last McDonald’s breakfast innovation I covered here on Sporked, we’re here to talk about a new sauce on a classic sandwich. Let’s find out whether this new Honey Brown Butter sauce can elevate the classic Bacon, Egg & Cheese Biscuit sandwich (plus what might be the world’s first review of a custom vegetarian variant).

articles.headline: Popular Salad Chain Addresses Cyclospora Outbreak Concerns
articles.author: Anthony Thompson
articles.summary: Sweetgreen is reassuring customers that the salad chain has not been linked to the ongoing cyclospora outbreak that has sickened thousands of people across the United States. “We’ve seen the news, and we know you have questions. We’re on it,” Sweetgreen said in a post on X. “Sweetgreen has NOT been identified in connection with the current cyclospora outbreak, but our food safety experts continue to monitor the situation closely.” The company said food safety is central to its daily operations and highlighted its sourcing and safety practices “from farm to restaurant.”

articles.headline: A Classic Chicken Franchise’s Path To More Than 250 Locations
articles.summary: The great chicken wars have not been won. The market is as competitive as ever, with franchises and brands seeking to carve out their own niche in the market. Golden Chick, a Texas-grown concept, is about to celebrate 60 years and has more than 250 locations. With consistent growth over the past few years, it is now on the path to open 27–30 additional locations in 2026 and is aiming to have 400 locations by 2030. But what makes a chicken concept stand out for prospective operators, franchisees, and consumers? For Tony Eisermann, vice president of development at Golden Chick, it’s a commitment to food quality and support of franchisees. “We try not to chase the trends or the fads that are out there,” Eisermann says. “We want to focus on the fact that we have great options; tenders, bone-in chicken (fried and roasted), wonderful sides, and of course our Almost World-Famous Rolls that we will put up against anybody in the industry.”

articles.headline: Chick-fil-A Is Testing Spicy Chick-n-Strips
articles.author: Alicia Kelso
articles.summary: Chick-fil-A’s signature Chick-n-Strips are now available in a spicy version, but only at two restaurants and only for a limited time. The chain is testing the item at its Sandy Spring and Sprayberry restaurants in the Atlanta market from now through July 12, or while supplies last. They are available in restaurants and through delivery. Spicy Chick-n-Strips are made from the most tender part of the chicken breast, seasoned with a spicy blend of peppers, breaded and cooked in 100% refined peanut oil. They are available with the customers’ choice of dipping sauce as a 3-count, 4-count, or 10-count entrée, and can also be ordered as part of a meal.

articles.headline: For Sale: The Tough-Talkin’, Finger-Lickin’ Legacy Of Colonel Sanders
articles.author: Kim Severson
articles.summary: Nearly a half-century after his death, Harland Sanders has one of the most recognizable faces in the world. They dress statues of him in Santa Claus costumes in Japan, where his fried chicken is the must-have Christmas dinner. Fans in China, home to the most KFC restaurants, regard him as a respected elder. He’s a symbol of quality and cleanliness in Nigeria and Kenya. But at Blackwood Hall, the 19th-century plantation-style house in Shelbyville, Ky., where he once taught franchise owners how to pressure-cook chicken while his wife bagged his secret mix of 11 herbs and spices, people still remember the real Colonel Sanders: a generous, cantankerous perfectionist, with a talent for swearing, who regretted selling his company for $2 million in 1964.

articles.headline: More Michigan Lawsuits Accuse Taylor Farms, Taco Bell Of Negligence In Cyclospora Outbreak
articles.author: Ivy S. Fowler
articles.summary: Two more lawsuits against Taco Bell and Taylor Farms, the two companies linked to a cyclosporiasis outbreak in nine states, were filed last week. Nine total Michigan residents filed two separate lawsuits on Wednesday and Thursday against Taco Bell and Taylor Fresh Foods, owner of Taylor Fresh Farms, seeking financial compensation for damages caused by getting cyclosporiasis after eating Taco Bell, according to court documents. These suits come after a married couple from Durand, Mich., sued the two companies for $75, 000 on July 17 after they both ate at Taco Bell and later got cyclosporiasis, a parasitic infection caused by the parasite Cyclospora and results in watery, "explosive" diarrhea, fatigue, and loss of appetite.

articles.headline: Chipotle Opens First Restaurant In Mexico As Part Of Chain’s Global Expansion
articles.author: Sophia Compton
articles.summary: Chipotle Mexican Grill opened its first restaurant in Mexico this month as part of the fast-casual chain’s international growth strategy. The new location opened on July 16 in San Pedro Garza García, Nuevo León, part of the Monterrey metropolitan area, and is being operated in partnership with restaurant operator Alsea, according to a news release from Chipotle. “We are entering Mexico with deep respect for the country’s culinary heritage and a commitment to delivering the Chipotle experience with excellence,” Scott Boatwright, CEO of Chipotle, said in a statement.

articles.headline: Burger King Announces New Service Changes After Customer Complaints
articles.author: Maria Chamberlain
articles.summary: Burger King is rolling out two new initiatives aimed at improving the customer experience after gathering feedback from thousands of guests across the U.S. The fast food chain announced the launch of its new "Your Way Champion" role and a Whopper Guarantee, saying the changes were inspired by comments received through its customer Listening Initiative. Earlier this year, Burger King invited customers to share feedback directly with U.S. and Canada President Tom Curtis by phone and text. According to the company, many guests said they wanted someone in restaurants who could quickly resolve issues when they arise. In response, Burger King created the Your Way Champion, a restaurant leadership role focused on customer service.

articles.headline: Burger King Offering Free Whoppers To Unsatisfied Customers
articles.author: Zach Kaplan
articles.summary: If Burger King messes up your Whopper, the next one is on the house, according to the fast food chain’s new “Whopper Guarantee.” The company announced in a release this week that if the iconic burger “doesn’t meet a Guest’s expectations, the brand will not only continue to remake it on the spot, but they’ll offer the Guest’s next Whopper for free.”

articles.headline: Taco Bell’s $1 Enchirito Entices Customers After Parasite Scare
articles.author: Daniela Sirtori
articles.summary: Taco Bell’s lettuce-free burrito drenched in enchilada sauce helped the chain mitigate the impact of a parasite outbreak that has put off diners. On July 22, when the company started selling $1 Enchiritos for “the ones who’ve been riding with us,” transactions were down 1% compared with the prior week. That was an improvement from the double-digit declines registered each day between July 14 and July 21, according to data compiled by Bloomberg Second Measure.

articles.headline: How Wendy's Is Evolving Its Loyalty Program
articles.author: Jonathan Maze
articles.summary: People who love Frosties also apparently love tote bags and charm bracelets. Wendy’s in May and June released the first merchandise drops in its history, allowing members of its loyalty program to scoop up free tote bags, charm bracelets, soccer jerseys, and even a digital camera. They all went quickly. The 5,000 totes, 5,000 charm bracelets and 1,000 soccer jerseys were all gone within 90 seconds. The 20 Canon G2X cameras took just two seconds to be claimed.

articles.headline: This AI Restaurant Trend Has Us Losing Our Appetites (Seriously, Stop)
articles.author: Jonathan Maze
articles.summary: When techno-evangelists talk about artificial intelligence, they talk about it like a natural resource. According to them, not using AI would be like living near a mighty river without fishing in it, or using it to irrigate your crops. (That's why Mississippi grows so much rice.) But that's not what AI is. AI is a product, or a series of products, designed by some of the wealthiest and most powerful corporations in history, and sold to us with the aggression of a drug dealer in a D.A.R.E. public service announcement. We're told that it can do anything, that it can make every task easier, that it's already here, and there's no point in resisting it. And maybe, to some extent, that's true. But when we see ugly, tasteless AI art used to advertise restaurants, we can't help but push back.

articles.headline: Converge AI Brings Its AI-Native Workspace To Multi-Unit Restaurants
articles.summary: Ask any multi-unit operator where the real bottleneck lives, and the answer usually isn't a lack of software. It's the opposite. Corporate teams are drowning in tools that don't talk to each other—campaign calendars in one system, guest feedback in another, franchisee comms in a third—while lean staffs try to keep dozens or even hundreds of locations moving in sync. That gap is exactly where Converge AI is now planting its flag. On July 23, 2026, the Rancho Palos Verdes, Calif.–based company outlined how its AI-native workspace can support restaurant marketing, operations, and guest engagement—advancing follow-up conversations with industry leaders and multi-unit operators coming out of CREATE 2026, the Nation's Restaurant News foodservice conference held at Terranea Resort.

articles.headline: What AI? Chili's Spends Big On WiFi And Tablets Instead Of Tokens
articles.author: Alex Bitter
articles.summary: Chris Caldwell is more focused on tablets these days than AI tokens. The chief information officer of Chili's parent company, Brinker International, has spent his 2½ years in the role figuring out how to overhaul WiFi systems at restaurants and replace thousands of handheld devices that waitstaff use to take customers' orders, he told Business Insider. Many restaurants are adding AI to their operations. At Starbucks and Burger King, for instance, AI agents are listening to drive-thru orders and fetching recipes for baristas.

articles.headline: How A.I. Can Strengthen Restaurants While Keeping Hospitality Human
articles.author: Johann Moonesinghe
articles.summary: Every major technological revolution begins with tools. Its lasting impact comes when those tools become infrastructure. Amazon did not simply make shopping more convenient. It reshaped the infrastructure of commerce. Google did not merely improve search. It became infrastructure for organizing information. Artificial intelligence is beginning a similar transition. The most important question is no longer what A.I. can generate, but what A.I. can make possible for industries that have never had access to real intelligence at scale. Restaurants are among America’s largest employers and most important small businesses. They are also unusually complex operations, balancing thin margins, rising labor costs, volatile demand and highly perishable inventory.

articles.headline: Domino’s Found A Growth Engine Beyond Just Pizza—And It Just Helped It Beat Expectations
articles.author: Amaya Nichole
articles.summary: Earlier this week, Domino’s Pizza reported quarterly revenue that beat Wall Street’s expectations. Domino’s supply-chain business—the division responsible for producing and distributing ingredients, dough, and equipment to its franchise stores—was the primary driver behind the company’s latest results. That segment grew in part due to higher order volumes from stores. As a result, the Ann Arbor, Michigan-based company reported second-quarter revenue of $1.19 billion, an increase of 4.3 percent and slightly ahead of the $1.18 billion analysts had projected, with supply-chain revenue alone climbing 6.5 percent to $731.7 million.

articles.headline: How 4 QSR Chains Sped Up Franchised Growth In H1
articles.author: Aneurin Canham-Clyne
articles.summary: While several major brands have closed large numbers of stores in 2026, some small and medium-sized restaurant chains spent H1 speeding up their franchised growth by signing new deals, adding new partners and targeting new markets or real estate types. Many of these deals were in subsectors where major restaurant chains have also seen growth — chicken, sandwiches and snacks/desserts. Take a look at Restaurant Dive’s analysis of how a handful of smaller players, international brands and challenger chains have worked to accelerate development.

articles.headline: Jersey Mike’s Beats Chick-fil-A As America’s Most Satisfying Fast Food Chain
articles.author: James Howard
articles.summary: If you are eating fast food on a U.S. road trip this summer, a new independent study says there is one chain worth adding to your route — and it is not the one you have been defaulting to for a decade. Jersey Mike's Subs dethroned Chick-fil-A this year as the top-rated quick-service restaurant in America, earning a score of 84 out of 100 in the 2026 ACSI Restaurant and Food Delivery Study — the first time any brand has led the American Customer Satisfaction Index's fast-food category since Chick-fil-A took the crown more than 11 years ago. And the chain's momentum goes further than a single survey: Jersey Mike's this week launched a Wall Street roadshow for a planned NYSE listing under the ticker JMKE, with a previously reported target valuation of more than $12 billion and an expected listing date of approximately July 30. For road-trip travelers, both developments carry a practical message: there are now more than 3,300 Jersey Mike's locations across the U.S., expansion is accelerating, and what was once a regional East Coast favorite is fast becoming a national road-trip staple.

articles.headline: Missouri Survey: More Than Half Of Restaurants Saw Fewer Customers During World Cup
articles.author: Beth Carlson
articles.summary: In a survey from the Missouri Restaurant Association, over half of businesses reported lower customer turnout than expected during the World Cup. Nearly six out of ten said the World Cup had an overall negative impact on business and revenue. One of the restaurants that felt the pain is Blvd Tavern in the Crossroads. Owner Derich Carlson said summer is always a slower season but had less business than in years prior during the World Cup season. "We were kind of led to believe that it was going to be like the entire six weeks. And it was more so like the day before and like the day after, and not on match day," Carlson said.

articles.headline: Restaurant Pros Debate: Are Diners ‘Guests’ Or ‘Customers’?
articles.author: Patricia Kelly Yeo
articles.summary: Simon Kim, the restaurateur behind Michelin-starred Cote (New York City, Miami, Las Vegas, Singapore) and the upscale fried chicken restaurant Coqodaq in New York City, believes diners should be called “customers.” Kim’s Gracious Hospitality Management, which also operates three-in-one cocktail den Bar Chimera and soon-to-debut omakase concept Sushi Yoshitake, uses “customers” exclusively while training its staff. According to Kim, who was born and raised in Seoul, the approach to hospitality there is different.

articles.headline: Apollo Group To Acquire Norway’s Fly Chicken Chain To Roll Out KFC Brand
articles.author: Umesh Ellichipuram
articles.summary: KFC franchisor Apollo Group, in collaboration with MM Group, is in the process of acquiring Norwegian fast casual restaurant chain Fly Chicken to launch the KFC brand in the country. Apollo Group plans to convert most of Fly Chicken’s 19 locations across Norway into KFC restaurants. In addition to the conversions, the franchisor intends to open further KFC sites in the country over the next five years. With this move, Norway will become the fifth market where the Apollo Group runs KFC restaurants under a franchise agreement. Alongside the acquisition, Apollo Group plans to invest €20m ($22m) in the Norwegian market over the coming five years. Following completion of the deal, Fly Chicken’s co-founder and CEO Ronny Gjøse will remain in his role.

articles.headline: Taco Bell Offering Another $1 Lettuce-Free Item. See New Promotion
articles.author: Drew Pittock
articles.summary: Taco Bell is offering another $1 lettuce-free option on July 28, following the success of last week’s $1 Enchirito promotion and the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak. In a social media post, Taco Bell announced it will be selling its Mexican Pizza for $1 at participating locations. The fast-food chain's Mexican Pizza features beef and beans between two flour tortillas topped with Mexican pizza sauce, cheese and diced tomatoes. It usually costs $5.39 to $6.99 depending on location. Here’s what you should know about Taco Bell's $1 Mexican Pizza promotion. Taco Bell announced that participating locations will sell its Mexican Pizza menu item for $1 through 11:59 p.m. PT on July 28. The promotion follows a similar $1 Enchirito offer that was available July 22.

articles.headline: Clinton Twp. Couple Sues Taco Bell Over Cyclosporiasis
articles.author: Kara Berg
articles.summary: A Clinton Township couple is suing Taco Bell and Taylor Farms after the couple says they contracted cyclosporiasis from eating infected lettuce from the restaurant, which was sourced from Taylor Farms. Karl and Gina Hercula, of Clinton Township, became ill in July after eating Taco Bell meals containing shredded lettuce in June, according to the lawsuit, filed July 22 in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan. The lawsuit alleges Taylor Farms and Taco Bell owed it to the Herculas to prepare, distribute and sell food that was fit for human consumption and did not have parasites or other substances on it that would affect their health.

articles.headline: 7 Beloved Menu Items From The ’90s That Vanished From Chain Restaurants
articles.author: Leah Groth
articles.summary: One of my favorite 1990s meals was a big bucket of fried chicken with the corn on the cob soaked in butter that came inside that yellow plastic bag. KFC corn on the cob disappeared in the early 2000s, and people are still talking about it. “That tasted soo good slathered in butter..nom nom,” one Redditor. Taco Bell registered the name Enchirito with the United States Patent and Trademark Office way back in May 1970, describing it as a “Combination Enchilada And Burrito” and it was a mainstay on the menu until discontinued in 1993. The Wendy’s salad bar, aka The SuperBar, was another popular feature in the fast food chain during the 1990s. “The SuperBar arguably was discontinued because it was too popular, and thus became harder to keep clean and to maintain,” a person says. “I miss the salad bar too. I would make a special trip to Wendy’s for lunch just for that salad bar,” another said.

articles.headline: Even Taco Bell Knows Bacon Makes Everything Better: Crispy Chicken Chipotle Bacon Melt Burrito Review
articles.author: Michael Palan
articles.summary: Most everyone loves the taste of bacon, including those who don't eat meat. In the 1960s, Betty Crocker did vegetarians a solid by introducing the bacon-free Bac*Os, allowing the familiar divine swine flavors be texture profiles to decorate the likes of salads, soups, and everything in between. Their popularity even gave rise to bacon bits ... made with actual bacon! In the middle of summer 2026, Taco Bell is changing the leafy lettuce subject by introducing Chipotle Bacon bits wrapped up in a cheesy burrito, headlined by its always seemingly disappearing, forever returning yummy Crispy Chicken Strips. Along for the ride is a dash of Avocado Ranch Sauce, and (gasp!) lettuce.

articles.headline: Chipotle Is Giving Away Free Chips And Guacamole—Here’s How To Claim Yours
articles.author: Grace Galante
articles.summary: Chipotle is giving away free chips and guacamole on Friday, July 31, and Saturday, Aug. 1! For the first time ever, the chain is giving customers the chance to score the free side in celebration of National Avocado Day on July 31. All customers have to do is order an entrée in the Chipotle app or on Chipotle.com on July 31 or Aug. 1 and use the code AVO2026 at checkout to get their free chips and guac! The Chipotle app is available on the App Store and Google Play. The chain is also giving away 80,000 free entrées until Wednesday, July 29! Earlier this month, Chipotle partnered with the PGA TOUR 2K25 video game for the Chipotle Hot Streak Quest, giving customers a chance to score codes for free entrées and double protein. First, you’ll have to buy the PGA TOUR 2K25 video game, if you don’t own it already, and complete the three themed chapters in MyCAREER mode. The chapters include in-game rewards like a taco-head putter and foil-themed golf attire.

articles.headline: Burger King’s New Paw Patrol Toys Include First Look At Dino Movie Characters
articles.author: Dani Meyering
articles.summary: As excitement builds for Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie, Burger King is giving young fans an early chance to meet the rescue pups — and two prehistoric newcomers — before they hit the big screen. The restaurant chain has launched a new limited-time Paw Patrol King Jr. Kids Meal at participating locations nationwide, with each meal including one of six collectible toys inspired by the upcoming film, which arrives in theaters on Aug. 14. The Burger King promotion arrives just weeks before “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie” debuts in theaters, offering one of the first opportunities for fans to collect merchandise based on the film. Each King Jr. Kids Meal includes a hamburger, cheeseburger, or Chicken Nuggets, plus a side, drink, and one randomly selected collectible toy. The promotion is available for a limited time while supplies last.

articles.headline: How AI Is Helping QSRs Improve Promotional Execution During Peak Traffic Seasons
articles.author: Scott Lasher
articles.summary: The most difficult stretches of each year for QSRs are peak traffic seasons—summer break, back-to-school, the holidays at the end of the year. Guests show up en masse while corporate pushes new, limited-time offers. The stress put on individual outposts is real, and the gap between what HQ has planned and what guests actually see has typically been viewed as an unavoidable cost of doing business. With AI, that’s starting to change. One photo and an AI model can do what the email chain never could. A team member can take a single image in the front of house, and then AI can identify whether the respective parts of the promotion have been executed: window cling, menu strip, register-area material. QSRs can be sure corporate knows the individual locations are matching the expected execution of the promotional plan.

articles.headline: AI Is Rewriting The Rules Of Restaurant Strategy — Here's How To Keep Up
articles.summary: Consumer behavior is shifting. Privacy expectations are tightening. Data regulations are evolving by the month. For restaurant leaders trying to make smart calls on site selection, marketing and operations, the ground is moving faster than the old playbook can keep pace with. That's exactly the challenge FastCasual.com's next webinar, "AI and the Future of Restaurants: From Foot Traffic to Predictive Insight," is designed to help solve. Joining FastCasual.com Publisher Cherryh Cansler for the conversation are two experts who approach the problem from different angles: AziraCEO Gladys Kong, a 20-plus-year veteran of data science and geolocation intelligence, and Goodway Group's Isabelle Soriano, a Senior Client Director who has spent nearly eight years building integrated marketing strategies for QSR and other major industries.

articles.headline: New Report Shows AI Is Creating A ‘Restaurant Profitability Gap’
articles.author: Kelly Beaton
articles.summary: A new survey illustrates that AI is becoming a game-changer for the foodservice industry. In its 2026 State of the Restaurant Industry: Mid-Year Report, the Restaurant365 management platform uncovered a notable difference in performance between restaurants using AI and those that are averse to the technology. Drawing upon survey responses from more than 420 restaurant operators, Restaurant365 found that 62% of those using AI for back-office functions reported reduced labor costs. “The real eye-opener is what we’re calling the ‘restaurant profitability gap,’” Restaurant365 executive Steve Demchuk told The Food Institute. “Back-office AI adoption has more than doubled since January, and the operators using it are reporting meaningfully better outcomes.” Operators using AI experienced stronger results across key profitability drivers such as food costs and operational efficiency.

articles.headline: McDonald’s Latest Breakfast Sandwich Adds A Sweet Twist
articles.author: Justin Boggs
articles.summary: For the second consecutive week, McDonald’s has announced a new menu item. This week, McDonald’s unveiled its Honey Brown Butter Bacon, Egg & Cheese Biscuit. The sandwich is similar to the chain’s bacon, egg and cheese biscuit, but includes honey brown butter on the biscuit for added flavor. McDonald’s said the new item will be available for a limited time at U.S. restaurants. “This savory-meets-sweet breakfast sandwich brings together salty, thick-cut applewood-smoked bacon, melty American cheese and a perfectly folded egg — all stacked on a warm buttermilk biscuit brushed with real butter and topped with Honey Brown Butter sauce,” McDonald’s said. The item has 490 calories, just 30 more than the standard bacon, egg and cheese biscuit. The new breakfast item comes as McDonald’s also rolls out a Caesar dipping sauce at participating restaurants for a limited time.

articles.headline: Report: Ohio Mcdonald’s Rank Among The Lowest In The Nation
articles.author: Stephanie Thompson
articles.summary: A report analyzing millions of McDonald’s customer reviews revealed that the chain’s Ohio locations received some of the lowest ratings in the nation. A study by Restaurant Furniture found customers in the Buckeye State gave the chain some of the lowest average ratings nationwide, according to a news release. Researchers analyzed 346,236 Google reviews across 193 Ohio locations, finding the chain earned an overall rating of 3.25 out of 5. The study examined Google reviews from the 10 most populated cities in each state. Researchers calculated a weighted average using each city’s number of locations and average rating to determine the highest- and lowest-rated McDonald’s in every state. Overall, Toledo had the state’s lowest-rated McDonald’s locations, with an average score of 3.06. The highest-rated restaurants were in northeast Ohio, with Parma averaging 3.38 and Lorain 3.37. “What stood out in Ohio was the range between cities,” said Nick Warren, head of ecommerce at Restaurant Furniture. “Parma scores 3.38 while Toledo sits at just 3.06, which suggests individual location management plays a huge role even within the same state.”

articles.headline: McDonald’s Decided You Are Not Worth Helping Anymore
articles.author: Daniel Kline
articles.summary: Starbucks has found the perfect mix of digital and human ordering. You can use the company’s app to place your complicated order and know it will be made exactly the way you want. And people who don’t want to use the app can stand in line or go through the drive-through to order from an actual human. It’s a simple formula that makes technology an option but doesn’t force it down people’s throats. McDonald’s has embraced technology, but at the expense of people. In many stores, it has replaced the human ordering option with kiosks. To make matters worse, those kiosks aren’t in any way intuitive, and they’re frustrating to use at best.

articles.headline: Chick-fil-A Temporarily Closes In Valley Ranch Town Center For Drive-Thru Remodel
articles.author: Emily Lincke
articles.summary: The Chick-fil-A location in Valley Ranch Town Center will be closed July 27-28 for renovations to the store's drive-thru, according to a July 25 social media post from the business. The restaurant is expected to reopen July 29. Chick-fil-A serves fried and grilled chicken sandwiches, nuggets and salads, according to the company's website. The restaurant also offers wraps, milkshakes, lemonade and waffle fries. The Chick-fil-A in VRTC also underwent a remodel in April 2025, as previously reported by Community Impact.

articles.headline: Culver’s, Raising Cane’s Chicken Fingers Construction Underway In Trussville
articles.author: Isaac Goffin
articles.summary: Two highly anticipated new to the market Trussville eateries are under construction and progressing. It was announced in February that Culver’s had closed on the property, but no timeline for construction had been had been set at the time. The, however, building is now well underway. The Wisconsin based burger restaurant will be located at 5905 Trussville Crossings Boulevard in the former BancorpSouth building across from the former Whataburger building just off of Chalkville Mountain Road. The restaurant opened in Sauk City, Wisconsin in 1984. They opened the first Alabama location in 2018. Culver’s is known for their ButterBurger, cheese curds and frozen custard. Representatives from Raising Cane’s appeared before the Trussville Design Review Committee in February to present plans for a new fast-casual restaurant at the former Pet Supplies Plus location on U.S. Highway 11.

articles.headline: KFC Founder Colonel Sanders’ Signature Bow Tie And Personal Planner Sell At Auction
articles.author: Dylan Lovan
articles.summary: KFC founder Colonel Sanders ' signature black bow tie, original cash register and dozens of other personal items sold Tuesday night in a public auction, while his former home and another restaurant he owned were up for auction later in the week. With his distinctive wardrobe and goatee, Harland Sanders built global brand recognition for the chain originally known as Kentucky Fried Chicken. He has remained the widely recognized face of the worldwide chain after his death in 1980. “Colonel Sanders was the original celebrity chef,” said Bill Menish, whose firm, The Menish Group, is conducting the auction. “The feedback has been worldwide, so we needed to have an auction that would cater to that worldwide audience.”

articles.headline: KFC Puts Its Country Fried Steak In The Value Spotlight
articles.author: Alicia Kelso
articles.summary: KFC is leveraging consumer trends toward comfort food by shining a spotlight on its Country Fried Steak, which rolled out to the broader system earlier this month. For a limited time, the chicken chain is offering a Country Fried Steak Meal for $4.99, including crispy fried steak covered in white gravy, gravy-covered mashed potatoes, coleslaw, and a warm biscuit. The deal is available on Wednesdays only at participating restaurants nationwide for a limited time. At KFC restaurants where the item was already on the menu, average daily Country Fried Steak orders jumped nearly 20% following its broader rollout, the company said. The lack of national promotion and its Wednesday-only availability at select locations has given it somewhat of a cult following among KFC regulars, and the company calls it one of its "best-kept secrets."

articles.headline: Taco Bell Is Offering A $1 Deal For Lettuce-Free Menu Item Amid Cyclosporiasis Outbreak
articles.author: Chiara Kim
articles.summary: Taco Bell is offering a $1 deal for one day only. The fast food chain, which recently stopped using lettuce from Taylor Farms amid links to a cyclosporiasis outbreak, is offering a $1 Mexican pizza deal on Tuesday, July 28, according to a post on its Instagram. The chain shared an image of the Mexican pizza, which features beef, beans, Mexican pizza sauce, tomatoes and cheese layered between and on top of crispy flour tortilla shells, with text overlaying that reads, “$1 mexican pizza. one day.” In the comments section, Taco Bell said the item is available for $1 plus tax at participating locations. Fans can score the deal in person or on the chain’s app or website — it’s limited to one deal per transaction, from 8 a.m. to 11:59 p.m. PT on July 28.

articles.headline: Wendy’s U.S. Closures And China Push Could Be A Game Changer For Wendy’s (WEN)
articles.author: Sasha Jovanovic
articles.summary: In recent months, Wendy’s has permanently closed multiple restaurants in Ohio amid ongoing U.S. sales challenges, while outlining plans to build as many as 1,000 locations in China over the next decade to reshape its footprint. This combination of domestic retrenchment and ambitious overseas expansion highlights management’s attempt to rebalance Wendy’s reliance on its core U.S. market. Next, we’ll examine how U.S. store closures and the China expansion push affect Wendy’s investment narrative and longer-term risk profile.

articles.headline: 4 Ordering Tips To Get The Best Wendy's Frosty
articles.author: Stacie Adams
articles.summary: Wendy's Classic Chocolate Frosty is just about perfect on its own, but certain ordering hacks take this legendary dessert to the next level. A Frosty is surprisingly adaptable, so most of our tips involve pairing it with other items. Lots of people get their kicks by dipping fries into their Frosty, but the dessert also mixes well with fountain drinks and coffee (hot or cold brew). We also stumbled upon a method for creating a fun combo Frosty, as well as a hack for getting more out of Wendy's bakery section. In the realm of fast-food desserts, Wendy's Frosty is iconic. A staple of the restaurant since the very first location opened, the creamy confection was modeled after a type of ice cream sold at an Ohio racetrack in the '60s. The Frosty was developed at the behest of restaurant founder Dave Thomas, who wanted a signature dessert that struck a balance between standard milkshakes and soft serve ice cream. Along with chocolate and vanilla, Wendy's also features a rotating selection of limited-time Frosty flavors with add-ins like flavored syrups, candy, and cookies.

articles.headline: The Founder Of Chipotle Says Customers Have ‘Slop Bowl’ Fatigue — Here’s What He Says Is The Next Big Thing
articles.author: Jonathan Small
articles.summary: Steve Ells invented the burrito bowl, and now he thinks people might be suffering from “slop bowl” fatigue. In an interview with the Wall Street Journal, the founder and former CEO of Chipotle talks about his new concept, Counter Service, a sandwich shop that launched last year in New York City and plans to expand to Charlotte and Dallas next year. Counter Service specializes in slow-roasted meats, homemade bread and made-in-house sauces and relishes. The concept pivots away from an earlier post-Chipotle venture, a vegan restaurant built around robotics. It uses technology that flags incorrectly assembled orders, part of a broader system predicting sales using traffic, transit and weather data. Ells says the appeal is in the details that most chains skip. “The pieces of meat are not perfectly shaped like the things you see in these chain sandwich places,” he said. “We’re making all of our sauces and relishes and garnishes. It’s difficult to do these things.” After 27 years eating Chipotle nearly every day, he says he now eats at Counter Service just as often.

articles.headline: Chipotle Is Handing Out Free Chips And Guac For 2 Days
articles.author: Khadrice Rollins
articles.summary: If you think you might be in the mood for a burrito or a bowl or some tacos on Friday, July 31 or Saturday, Aug. 1, make sure to leave some room for a side of chips and guacamole because Chipotle is handing out that combo for free. The company announced Monday that in honor of National Avocado Day on Friday, it would hold a two-day promotion. Customers can access the free chips and guac by purchasing an entrée on the Chipotle app and using code AVO2026 when checking out. The statement announcing the deal notes that customers should make sure to add a side of chips and guac to their meal in order for the promo code to work.

articles.headline: Burger King To Host Feed The Homeless Night
articles.author: Tony Nguyen
articles.summary: Burger King and New Growth Ministries will host a feeding-the-homeless event tonight. According to New Growth Ministries, the Feed the Homeless Night event will be on July 28 from 6-8 p.m. at the 425 N. West Bypass Burger King location. The ministry will also be accepting any donated hygiene and cooling items.

articles.headline: Burger King Welcomes Boomers. After A Fashion
articles.author: Emma Hall
articles.summary: Boomers are getting a rare moment in the spotlight in Buzzman Paris’ new campaign for Burger King. But it must surely have been Gen Z creatives who chose to dismiss the Boomer stage of life as bedevilled by aching backs, stiff knees, flying toupees and bald spots. To add insult to injury, the new Boomer King menu comes with collectible gifts inspired by naff 80s or 90s TV shows. The choice is between Saved by the Bell socks, a Knight Rider T-shirt, a Charmed mug or a Beverly Hills, 90210-branded glass. The soundtrack is a grating, generic-sounding 90s style TV theme tune.

articles.headline: Burger King Introduces “Your Way Champion” Role And Whopper Guarantee To Improve Customer Experience
articles.author: Neil Perry
articles.summary: Burger King has launched two new customer experience initiatives across its US business after gathering feedback from thousands of guests through its Listening Initiative. The company is introducing a new in-restaurant management role, the “Your Way Champion”, alongside a Whopper Guarantee aimed at improving order accuracy, food quality and customer satisfaction. The new initiatives are the latest phase of its brand transformation programme, which has focused on acting on customer feedback. The company introduced the changes after receiving thousands of calls and text messages from guests following its Listening Initiative, which invited customers to share feedback directly with President Tom Curtis. According to Burger King, customers consistently highlighted the importance of receiving accurate orders, high-quality food and a welcoming in-restaurant experience.

articles.headline: Why Chili’s Isn’t Going ‘All In’ On AI
articles.author: Isabelle Bousquette
articles.summary: In a world where artificial intelligence threatens to upend every facet of work and life, some things still remain sacred. And ordering Chili’s famous “Triple Dipper” is one of them. Chris Caldwell, chief information officer of Chili’s-owner Brinker International, said his senior leadership team agrees the restaurant chain is “not all in,” on AI. Instead, he’s spent his budget over the last two years revamping foundational in-restaurant tech, including newer Wi-Fi access points, payment systems, and devices for staff to fix what he said had become a broken experience for customers and workers. At the same time, he said he pulled back on sexy but ultimately useless initiatives, like robot servers, and has been selective about which generative AI applications are worth pursuing.

articles.headline: AI-Powered QSR Loyalty Programs
articles.author: Kalin Ned
articles.summary: Island Fin Poké Co. — the Florida-based fast-casual franchise inspired by Hawaiian culinary traditions and lifestyle — has launched a new loyalty program powered by the AI-native platform Hang. This development alows the company to move beyond the conventional earn-and-redeem points model to introduce gamified features. Through its partnership with Hang, Island Fin Poké Co. is able to introduce interactive mini-games, rotating monthly challenges known as Quests, and limited-time Mystery Boxes that reward guests for visits, referrals, and qualifying purchases. Prizes range from small perks like free toppings to substantial rewards such as complimentary poké bowls. This initiative, available through the brand's mobile app on both iOS and Android platforms, is designed to extend guest engagement beyond the physical restaurant walls. It makes for a more dynamic and entertaining relationship between the brand and its customers through elements of surprise.

articles.headline: Yelp Host Aims To Solve The Restaurant Industry’s Missed-Call Problem
articles.summary: Yelp has today expanded the capabilities of Yelp Host, enhancing its phone-based pickup ordering with more personalized and multilingual capabilities. By helping restaurants manage high call volumes without pulling employees away from in-person hospitality experiences, the company is now targeting the missed calls and fragmented experiences that can undermine restaurant service. CX leaders should now think about moving away from deploying AI without first considering whether it resolves customer needs accurately, contextually, and with an appropriate path to human support.

articles.headline: 7 Chick-Fil-A Breakfast Menu Items To Order And 4 To Skip
articles.author: Chelsea Falin
articles.summary: Chick-fil-A is a fast-food chicken chain giant that I personally adore for its lunch menu. In fact, my nearest restaurant is located central to everywhere I do my grocery shopping, making it one of my top-visited fast-food chains. But I've only visited during Chick-fil-A lunch hours, so its breakfast menu was entirely foreign to me, and I started wondering whether it would be as delicious as the lunch menu. Thankfully, I was given the opportunity to answer this question by trying 11 Chick-fil-A breakfast menu items and reporting my findings back here. My main question was, "Would I order this again?" When I was on the fence about something because of personal preferences, I considered whether other people would enjoy this. If the answer to one or both of those questions was "yes," I recommended them here. If the answer to both was "no," I recommended skipping them.

articles.headline: Is McDonald's Really Getting A 'Spongebob' X 'One Piece' Happy Meal Collab?
articles.author: Trey Alston
articles.summary: McDonald’s is rumored to be getting ready to launch Happy Meal toys that combine the worlds of SpongeBob SquarePants and One Piece. According to popular food leaker Snackolator, the company's New Zealand locations will be releasing Happy Meals that feature seven different toys combining the worlds of one of Nickelodeon’s most popular TV shows and one of the biggest manga properties in the world. Snackolator, who has a track record of accurately revealing food before it's officially announced, posted about the collab on July 28, unveiling seven different combo toys that should be released: SpongeBob and Luffy, Squidward and Sanji, Plankton and Usopp, Mrs. Puff and Linlin, Gary and Chopper, Mr. Krabs and Jinbe, and Larry and Franky.

articles.headline: Popeyes Names Anomaly Its US Creative Agency As Part Of A Broader Roster Overhaul
articles.author: Brian Bonilla
articles.summary: Popeyes has appointed Anomaly as its new U.S. creative agency of record as the chicken chain looks to sharpen its marketing around its core menu and value positioning following a prolonged stretch of sales declines.

articles.headline: Azle Is Finally Getting Its First Chick-Fil-A. Here’s When And Where
articles.author: Ella Gonzales
articles.summary: The Fort Worth suburb of Azle will finally get its fix of chicken nuggets, strips and sandwiches with its first ever Chick-fil-A opening at the end of July. The Chick-fil-A at 417 N.W. Parkway St. will be open for customers starting at 6 a.m. on Thursday, July 30. Any guests who visit dressed in cow spots can score a free entrée or kids’ meal in-store or through the drive-thru. “Azle is a close-knit community where people genuinely show up for one another, and it’s an honor to open the first Chick-fil-A restaurant here,” said local Owner-Operator Mike Tipton. “Our goal is for this restaurant to reflect exactly what makes this community special: a place where everyone feels welcomed and cared for, and where we can invest in our Team Members and the community we serve.” Tipton has owned and operated the Lake Worth Chick-fil-A since 2006, which was the closest Chick-fil-A location to Azle prior to the new restaurant opening.

articles.headline: National Chicken Finger Day With Raising Cane's
articles.summary: If you and your family are trying to come up with dinner plans, here’s an idea: chicken fingers. It’s National Chicken Finger Day, and Raising Cane’s is celebrating with free food, fun merch, and donations to support local kids. Joining us in the kitchen, sponsored by More for Less Remodeling, is Bryan Brzycki, Raising Cane’s Area Leader of Restaurants, with all the details. For more information, head to RaisingCanes.com.

articles.headline: The Best KFC Menu Item Isn’t The Fried Chicken, According To Customers
articles.author: Bailey Fink
articles.summary: Colonel Sanders’ signature blend of 11 herbs and spices may have been what put Kentucky Fried Chicken on the map, but today, the chain offers much more than its famous bucket of fried chicken. Fans frequent KFC for everything from its crispy chicken sandwiches and returning popcorn chicken to its Famous Bowls and tasty Southern sides. KFC might not have the biggest fast food menu on the market—you may recall the chain removed quite a few items in 2023—but there’s still a chance that you could be missing out on a menu item and meal deal that fans call “unbeatable.” Kentucky Fried Chicken has a menu item so elusive that you can only order it one day of the week, but it’s racked up quite the cult following. KFC customers love its Country Fried Steak.

articles.headline: Colonel Sanders’ ‘Secret’ KFC Recipe Planner Fetches $30K
articles.author: Bernadette Giacomazzo
articles.summary: A handwritten recipe once feared to be KFC’s most closely guarded secret just sold for $30,000. The list was tucked inside Colonel Sanders’ personal 1964 planner—and contained exactly 11 ingredients, immediately raising one very expensive question: Had the Kentucky Fried Chicken founder written down the chain’s supposedly untouchable formula? According to The Associated Press, the leather-bound planner topped a recent auction of Sanders’ belongings in Shelbyville, Kentucky. Along with the mystery recipe, its pages detail his relentless travel schedule as he crisscrossed the country building KFC into a national franchise.

articles.headline: 12 Discontinued Taco Bell Items That Deserve A Revival
articles.author: Amy Bell
articles.summary: Although there are constantly old items coming and going off the menu, there are still some great discontinued Taco Bell items that deserve a comeback that haven't yet had their day. In fact, there are quite a few tacos, burritos, gorditas, wraps, breakfast items, sauces, sides, and desserts that people still wish would make a return. While some items haven't been seen since as long ago as the 1980s, others are more recent limited-time menu offerings that were too good to not become permanent or have a limited return. Many of these items have online petitions for their return. Sometimes, it's possible to hack the menu to get something sort of similar, but if a sauce or the seasoning isn't right, it just doesn't hit the same.

articles.headline: US Diners Avoid Restaurants As Cyclosporiasis Fears Cut Lettuce Sales
articles.author: Tom Polansek, Anuja Bharat Mistry
articles.summary: U.S. consumers are steering clear of some restaurant chains and buying less lettuce in grocery stores as a ​multistate outbreak of a parasitic disease fuels confusion over what is safe to eat, according to foot traffic data and industry sources. The U.S. Food and ‌Drug Administration has linked the outbreak of cyclosporiasis to iceberg lettuce that was served at Taco Bell restaurants and sourced from privately held Taylor Farms' operations in central Mexico. But cases have continued to rise even after Taylor Farms said it removed all potentially affected products from the marketplace. The increase has stoked uncertainty and fears about other products that may be infecting people with the disease that causes explosive, watery diarrhea.

articles.headline: Major Burger Dining Chain Closes More Locations
articles.author: Kirk O’Neil
articles.summary: The nation’s No. 2 burger chain, Wendy’s, is continuing its Project Fresh turnaround strategy, that it launched in 2025, which calls for the company to shutter underperforming locations. Wendy’s in late July 2026 abruptly closed a restaurant at 4003 Wilmington Pike in Kettering, Ohio, with a sign posted on its front door which read: “This location is permanently closed.” The sign invited customers to visit its nearby store at 1880 E. Dorothy Lane, about 1.5 miles away, according to WDNT-TV. The Kettering closing was the second Wendy’s closure in the Dayton area in the last four months, as the chain closed a location in Moraine, Ohio, in March 2026, according to the Dayton Business Journal. Wendy’s has not listed any other locations that are currently scheduled for closing.

articles.headline: Chipotle Mexican Grill Posts Higher Sales, Driven By New Restaurant Openings
articles.author: Grace Yoon
articles.summary: Chipotle Mexican Grill raised its comparable sales guidance as it posted higher sales in its second quarter, fueled by new restaurant openings. The Mexican-inspired fast-casual chain reported a profit of $403.5 million, or 32 cents a share, compared with $436.1 million, or 32 cents a share, a year earlier.

articles.headline: Two Broome Burger King Locations Closing For Makeovers
articles.author: Bob Joseph
articles.summary: The grills at a couple of Burger King restaurants in the Binghamton area will be shut down for weeks for renovation work. Employees say the Burger King locations on Ash Road in Vestal and East Main Street in Endwell are expected to be closed for at least a month and perhaps as long as two months for the modernization projects. Representatives of the franchise operator recently discussed details of the renovations at meetings of the town of Vestal and town of Union planning boards. Both restaurants are scheduled to close at 5 p.m. Friday. Similar remodeling work at other New York state Burger King locations has taken four to six weeks to complete.

articles.headline: Is The Whopper Actually 100% Beef?
articles.author: Bridget Sharkey
articles.summary: Since its debut in 1957, the Burger King Whopper has been a fast-food favorite. In fact, it is estimated that 2.1 billion Whoppers are sold globally every year. But is the iconic flame-grilled burger actually made with 100% beef? It certainly is. Although you can customize your Whopper in over 200,000 ways, there is one thing that won't change: The burger patty will always be made with 100% beef. However, curious customers may have a hard time sourcing the origin of that beef.

articles.headline: Taco Bell Expands Voice AI To Nearly 900 Restaurants
articles.author: Bernadette Heier
articles.summary: Taco Bell has expanded its voice AI technology to more than 890 U.S. restaurants across 38 states as it deepens its partnership with voice AI provider Omilia. The companies first partnered in 2023. The voice AI takes customer orders at the drive-thru and adjusts to each restaurant’s menu, inventory levels and limited-time offers. “Omilia’s Voice AI gives us the ability to ease team members’ workloads and provides them the flexibility to engage with customers in a more meaningful way,” Dane Mathews, global chief digital and technology officer at Taco Bell, said in a statement. “Omilia’s platform has proven itself at scale in select U.S. restaurants, and continuing this strategic partnership supports our long-term digital and tech strategy.”

articles.headline: AI Is Fueling A Boom In Bogus Restaurant Websites
articles.author: Joe Guszkowski
articles.summary: When you Google “Golden Corral menu prices,” the first source cited in Google’s AI overview is the website golden-corral.us. The site is loaded with information about Golden Corral, including prices, a nutrition calculator, and even a nifty “AI buffet plate builder” tool. But it has no official connection to the buffet chain. “Golden-corral.us is an independent resource and is not affiliated with Golden Corral,” reads the fine print at the bottom of the site. “This website is for informational purposes only.”

articles.headline: Heytruffle Lands Funding To Scale Its Human-Monitored Restaurant AI Concierge Nationwide
articles.summary: When the dining room is slammed and the host stand is buried, the phone is usually the first casualty. That ringing line at the front desk represents reservations, catering leads, private-event inquiries, and pickup orders — real revenue slipping through the cracks every peak-hour rush. A Fort Lauderdale-based startup thinks the answer isn't another dashboard for operators to babysit, but a fully managed service that simply handles the call. Heytruffle, a managed AI phone concierge built for multi-location restaurant groups, has raised new funding from New York-based Preface Ventures. The company also unveiled a rebrand — it was formerly known as RestoHost — and says the capital will fuel a nationwide expansion across the United States. The timing tracks with where the money is going. In a 2025 Deloitte study, 82 percent of restaurant executives said they planned to increase their AI investment — though the report noted that industry adoption still lags the appetite. A separate 2025 Toast survey of more than 700 operators found that 86 percent were comfortable using AI.
