articles.headline: McDonald’s Decided You Are Not Worth Helping Anymore
articles.author: Daniel Kline
articles.summary: Starbucks has found the perfect mix of digital and human ordering. You can use the company’s app to place your complicated order and know it will be made exactly the way you want. And people who don’t want to use the app can stand in line or go through the drive-through to order from an actual human. It’s a simple formula that makes technology an option, but doesn’t force it down people’s throats. McDonald’s has embraced technology, but at the expense of people. In many stores, it has replaced the human ordering option with kiosks. To make matters worse, those kiosks aren’t in any way intuitive, and they’re frustrating to use at best.

articles.headline: McDonald’s Latest Breakfast Sandwich Adds A Sweet Twist
articles.author: Justin Boggs
articles.summary: For the second consecutive week, McDonald’s has announced a new menu item. This week, McDonald’s unveiled its Honey Brown Butter Bacon, Egg & Cheese Biscuit. The sandwich is similar to the chain’s bacon, egg and cheese biscuit, but includes honey brown butter on the biscuit for added flavor. McDonald’s said the new item will be available for a limited time at U.S. restaurants. The new breakfast item comes as McDonald’s also rolls out a Caesar dipping sauce at participating restaurants for a limited time. McDonald’s described the sauce as “a creamy, garlicky parmesan blend infused with notes of lemon that’s giving fan-favorite chicken items a glow-up this summer.”

articles.headline: Church’s Texas Chicken Secures Funding For ‘Next Stage Of Growth'
articles.author: Alicia Kelso
articles.summary: Church’s Texas Chicken just received a growth equity investment from Golub Capital that will ensure the 74-year-old brand keeps pace with the fast-growing chicken category. The undisclosed investment is aimed at accelerating the company’s “next phase of growth,” including the expansion of its remodel program, which it says has generated sales increases. The funding will also be used to accelerate new company-operated restaurant openings and other initiatives supporting brand and franchisee growth. Church’s currently has more than 1,500 restaurants across the U.S. and more than 25 international markets. Domestically, it finished 2025 with over $861 million in sales and 770 locations. In November, Church’s named Bobby Morena to the chief development officer role to continue its U.S. expansion.

articles.headline: Wingstop Believes Better Value Messaging Can Reignite Traffic
articles.summary: Wingstop has spent recent years proving it can outgrow the industry through unit expansion, surging brand awareness, and a product that consistently commanded premium pricing. The second quarter showed the limits of that formula in today’s consumer environment. Same-store sales declined 7.5 percent as the chain’s core guests pulled back on spending. AUV was $1.89 million, down from $2.11 million in Q2 2025. The result missed the company’s expectations and prompted executives to rethink how Wingstop communicates value, even as leadership argued the brand’s long-term trajectory hasn’t changed. The brand pointed to pressure on lower-income households—not weakening demand for the concept itself—as the primary obstacle.

articles.headline: Your Restaurant Pricing Strategy Isn’t Working Anymore. Here’s What Is.
articles.summary: For the past few years, the simple restaurant playbook has leaned into raising prices to boost revenue. That’s not working anymore. In many cases, price increases are actually suppressing growth by weighing on traffic and comparable sales (comps). The National Restaurant Association forecasts just 1.3 percent real sales growth this year, and Black Box data reported negative traffic in late 2025 and early 2026. The industry is still experiencing minimal growth, but yesterday’s drivers of growth are mostly gone. U.S. consumer sentiment over the last few months has been hovering near historic lows. Financially stressed consumers are looking sharply at discretionary spending and questioning purchases when the price doesn’t meet or exceed their expectations of value. In restaurants, this doesn’t mean consumers won’t spend on premium concepts; rather, it makes them less willing to pay for middle-of-the-road experiences.

articles.headline: KFC Customers Are Calling This Returning Item '1000x Better Than The Nuggets'
articles.author: Alia Ali
articles.summary: Sometimes the best part of fried chicken is not the chicken itself, but the crispy batter that surrounds it. Chicken tenders and nuggets increase the ratio of batter to chicken due to their smaller size. However, the highest ratio of batter to chicken is in the form of popcorn chicken. Popcorn chicken is essentially bite-sized pieces of chicken battered and deep-fried, resulting in a crispy, chicken-y bite. And customers are calling them the best returning fast food item of July 2026. Folks on social media have been celebrating the occasion by posting photos and thoughts on the return of this coveted snack. Over on Reddit, a self-proclaimed KFC employee noted, "They're so good, 1000x better than the nuggets.

articles.headline: Taco Bell’s Plan To Win Back Customers After Cyclospora Illness Outbreak
articles.author: Heather Haddon
articles.summary: Taco Bell has a battle plan to bring back customers after a parasitic outbreak was linked to lettuce served at its restaurants. The plan includes $1 Mexican Pizzas and limited-time offers such as butter chicken tacos. While health authorities linked an outbreak of cyclospora-related illnesses to product giant Taylor Farms, the fast-food standout has been hurt by people reporting explosive diarrhea and stomach cramping after dining at the chain’s locations.

articles.headline: Taco Bell Adding Another Location To St. Johns County Expansion Plans
articles.author: J. Brooks Terry
articles.summary: Taco Bell is adding another St. Johns County location to its regional expansion plans, marking a fourth proposed location, in addition to three already open in the county. The St. Johns River Water Management District began reviewing an environmental resource permit preapplication July 29 for a Taco Bell at U.S. 1 and Ponce Island Drive, just north of downtown St. Augustine. With the site being undeveloped, an ERP regulates construction and development to prevent flooding, protect water quality and preserve wetlands. The restaurant is planned on a portion of a 12.3-acre parcel owned by Ponte Vedra-based Sea Pine Equity Partners through Ponce Commercial LLC.

articles.headline: Wendy's Hands North America Comms Remit To Ruder Finn
articles.author: Nathan Cole
articles.summary: Ruder Finn has been selected as Wendy's North American communications agency of record following a competitive review, adding a large restaurant brand to the independent agency's consumer and reputation portfolio. Agnostic, Ruder Finn's strategic partner in Canada, will support Wendy's communications in that market. The brief is not a narrow media relations assignment. Wendy's said the model will connect brand marketing, corporate reputation, executive visibility, creator and influencer engagement, cultural relevance, strategic storytelling, issues management, and stakeholder communications across the United States and Canada.

articles.headline: 5 Chain Restaurants Famous For Their Ranch, According To Diners
articles.author: Jess Kelly
articles.summary: Wendy’s has a variety of sauces that people love dipping those nuggets and fries into. “Wendy’s Ghost Pepper Ranch,” a Reddit commenter said, discussing the best ranch available at chain restaurants. “This is by far the best. All other answers are wrong,” another said. The website backs up their dip quality, saying “Wendy’s sauces are premium. No shortcuts. No fillers. No sad dips. Just straight-up flavor mic drops.”

articles.headline: Chipotle’s Efforts To Engage Customers With Rewards In-Restaurant Pay Off
articles.author: Kristen Doerer
articles.summary: Chipotle has grown its Chipotle Rewards membership to 23 million active members since relaunching the loyalty program in April, CEO Scott Boatwright said on a Q2 2026 earnings call Wednesday. That accounts for 9.5% growth, according to loyalty membership data shared at launch. A main goal of the revamped Chipotle Rewards is to increase in-restaurant participation, as only about 20% of in-restaurant transactions utilize rewards, according to Boatwright. The company introduced menu panels, QR codes and team member engagement, which drove a nearly 20% step-up in daily enrollments since launch. “Encouragingly, in-store loyalty comps have outpaced order-ahead loyalty comps since the relaunch, reinforcing our belief that simplifying the in-restaurant rewards experience can meaningfully increase engagement over time,” Boatwright said on the call.

articles.headline: New Drinks, Burritos And Perks Help Chipotle And Starbucks Beat Cautious Consumers
articles.author: Daniela Sirtori, Redd Brown
articles.summary: Consumers’ reluctance to spend is no match for fruity refreshers and chipotle honey chicken burritos. Two of the largest US restaurant companies, Starbucks Corp. and Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc., both raised their guidance on Wednesday after stronger-than-expected quarters. Sales at both chains were bolstered by trendy new menu items and revamped loyalty programs. The results show that diners are still willing to open their wallets to eat out if the prices and flavors are right. They also offer hope to consumer companies as rising gas prices squeeze budgets and stoke fears that diners will cut back even more on restaurant outings. Companies including Procter & Gamble Co. and PepsiCo Inc. have said that consumers are retrenching.

articles.headline: The Burger King Baby Burgers Introduce Slider-Sized Versions Of Sandwiches
articles.author: Amy Duong
articles.summary: The Burger King Baby Burgers expand the chain's menu with miniature takes on three signature sandwiches following a social media campaign built around a pregnancy announcement theme. The lineup includes the Baby Whopper, Baby Cheese Bacon, and Baby Rodeo, each served on a brioche-style bun and available in packs of three or six. The launch reimagines familiar Burger King menu items in a smaller, shareable format without changing their core flavor profiles. The Baby Whopper features a flame-grilled beef patty with mayonnaise, lettuce, tomato, and pickles, while the Baby Cheese Bacon adds cheese and bacon. The Baby Rodeo rounds out the range with barbecue-inspired flavors. Introduced by Burger King Dominican Republic through a teaser campaign on social media, the Burger King Baby Burgers bring the brand's signature burgers to a slider-sized format while retaining the ingredients and preparation associated with the original sandwiches.

articles.headline: Chipotle’s Operational Reset Is Driving Clear Results
articles.summary: Chipotle first revealed its Recipe for Growth turnaround plan in February, and the impact has been swift. After exceeding expectations in Q1 with positive same-store sales and transactions, the fast casual did the same in the second quarter, with comps rising 2.2 percent and transactions increasing 1 percent. It was Chipotle’s best same-store sales performance since Q4 2024. AUV was at $3.102 million, up from $3.094 million in Q1. The company saw outsized improvement from younger consumers and lower-income guests, two cohorts the brand has struggled with as of late. Momentum carried into early July, but sales have softened in recent weeks by roughly 200 basis points because of a multistate cyclospora outbreak that has sickened thousands. Chipotle’s products have not been linked to the outbreak, which has been traced to iceberg lettuce—an ingredient the chain does not serve.

articles.headline: Fast-Food Execs Keep Pushing For More AI Systems, But Fail To See The Big Picture: Customers Still Want Humans
articles.author: Joshua Hong
articles.summary: Fast-food chains have spent the past several years racing to automate everything from drive-through ordering to burger flipping using AI. McDonald’s and Wendy’s have continued to experiment with AI ordering systems, forcing restaurants to answer more fundamental questions than whether robots can make fries or take orders. With the introduction of ArchIQ by McDonald’s earlier this year as part of its new initiative “McDonald’s > NEXT,” the fast-food giant is introducing AI-powered chatbots at its drive-through locations. Wendy’s has also implemented AI-powered drive-through systems since 2023, under its FreshAI program. In its 2026 first quarter earnings report, Wendy’s CFO Ken Cook said he wants to continue developing the digital experience. “We are continuing to invest in the end-to-end digital experience, leveraging consumer insights to drive frequency and engagement in the app,” he said in the conference call, “while expanding payment options at checkout to create a more seamless experience and improve conversion.”

articles.headline: Would You Like Fries With Those Prompts? Operators Using AI Are Cutting Food, Labor, Other Costs
articles.author: Teresa Buyikian
articles.summary: Restaurant operators utilizing AI are finally seeing the benefits across multiple key profitability drivers, per a new report from tech platform Restaurant365. The "2026 State of the Restaurant Industry Mid-Year Report" found operators that have embraced AI are actually seeing measurable differences across food and labor costs, as well as operational efficiency. Of the of operators currently using AI in at least one back-office function (62%), 61% said they have seen reduced food costs since implementation. Sixty-two percent of them also saw reduced labor costs, while 88% reported AI was “saving time every week.”

articles.headline: Chick-Fil-A Set To Open First Stanislaus County Location In Turlock
articles.author: Elizabeth Perez
articles.summary: Stanislaus County will soon get to “Eat Mor Chikin” in Turlock. Chick-fil-A is set to have its grand opening in Turlock on Aug. 6. It will be the Chick-fil-A's first location in Stanislaus County. The fast-food chicken sandwich chain will be located in the new Turlock Marketplace development at the southwest corner of Tuolumne Road and Countryside Drive, according to city officials. Chick-Fil-A will be the first business to open in the almost 30-acre commercial center. The new location will adhere to the standard Monday to Saturday hours, being open from 6:30 a.m. to 11 p.m. every day except Sundays, when it is are closed. Residents are encouraged and invited to attend the grand opening on Thursday, August 6. Guests wearing cow-print clothing, cow costumes and cow themed attire can receive one complimentary entrée or Kid’s Meal.

articles.headline: 'Best Year Yet' | Gray Dairy Queen Raises Record-Breaking $250,000 On Miracle Treat Day
articles.author: Olivia Dunne
articles.summary: Gray's Dairy Queen took part in another sweet and successful Miracle Treat Day on Thursday. The busiest Dairy Queen in the world raised a record-breaking $250,000 for the Beverly Knight Olson Children's Hospital in Macon. The store took part in the national fundraising campaign for their sixth year Thursday, and donated every dollar made to the children's hospital. Store owner Justin Kelly announced the record-breaking campaign on social media. 13WMAZ originally reported the total as $245,000. However, Kelly confirmed another donor came forward after he announced the total. "The town is really bought in on this, and I believe this is gonna be the best year yet," Kelly said. Central Georgians hit the road by the hundreds to take part in the tradition, and drive-thru traffic often spilled onto West Clinton Street. Sharonda Williams says she had to come back when the crowds quieted down after she was met with heavy traffic Thursday morning.

articles.headline: Raising Cane's Is Launching Limited-Edition Megan Moroney Cups For Her Cloud 9 Tour
articles.author: Cris Tolomia
articles.summary: Raising Cane's is releasing two limited-edition collector's cups tied to country singer Megan Moroney's Cloud 9 Tour, with both items available starting Thursday. The first is the Rhinestone Tumbler, a purple rhinestone-covered cup that holds 24 ounces and retails for $19.99. The design traces back to a custom cup created exclusively for Moroney when she first partnered with Raising Cane's at an event in Athens, Georgia. After fans expressed interest in purchasing one, Raising Cane's owner and founder Todd Graves made it available to the public. It can be purchased in-store or through RaisingCanesGear.com while supplies last. A portion of each tumbler sale — $2 per unit — benefits the Megan Moroney Foundation, an organization dedicated to kindness, anti-bullying efforts, and mental health advocacy.

articles.headline: Fast Food Restaurants Are Eating Up The High Cost Of Beef
articles.summary: With ground beef prices topping $7 a pound for the first time, major fast-food chains are absorbing the cost instead of raising prices. More than half of Americans cite value menus as their top reason for choosing a restaurant. NBC News' Allie Canal reports.

articles.headline: 8 Fast-Food Toys Every Millennial Begged Their Parents To Buy
articles.author: Chelsea Thatcher
articles.summary: There are a lot of toys today that have us adults thinking, "I wish they had thought of that when I was a kid!" But one category of toys has younger generations envious of millennials: the fast-food toy. Today's kids' meal toys are pretty lame compared to what we had as kids. Their low quality is laughable next to the '90s figurines that could have been confused for toy store purchases. The fast food toys of today will never be as cool as the ones we got in the '90s because, sadly, companies don't make them like they used to. But we can reminisce about some of the best kids' meal toys that every millennial just had to have.

articles.headline: Fast-Food Chain Off The Hook Expands To Hattiesburg, First MS Location
articles.author: Davis Wilson
articles.summary: A Louisiana-based fast-food restaurant is crossing state lines for the first time and opening a Mississippi location in Hattiesburg. Off the Hook, a Cajun fast-food chain, opened its first restaurant in Thibodaux, Louisiana, in 2012 and has since opened eight more locations, all of which are in Louisiana. It's 10th location, in Hattiesburg, is slated to open in fall 2026 at 6218 U.S. Highway 98, which is currently home to a Golden Chick restaurant that neighbors a Starbucks. "As we have grown throughout South Louisiana, we have remained committed to the recipes, ingredients and relationships that shaped our brand," Off the Hook said in a press release. "The Hattiesburg restaurant marks an exciting milestone as our first location outside of Louisiana, but the food and experience will stay true to where we started."

articles.headline: 6 Restaurant Chains With The Best Bacon, According To Chefs
articles.author: Heather Newgen
articles.summary: Few fast-food chains earn praise from professional chefs for their bacon, but Wendy’s stands out for its preparation method and reliable quality. Steve Ingber, Executive Chef & Owner, MileHighCook, says those details make a noticeable difference in the finished product. “Wendy’s is the only major chain that cooks their bacon Applewood-smoked and thick-cut in the oven rather than pre-cooked and reheated, and that matters,” he says. “You get actual rendered fat, a real snap when you bite it, and a smoke flavor that survives sitting under a bun. Most fast-food bacon goes limp and greasy because it’s steamed back to life; Wendy’s keeps structure and char.” He adds, “As a chef, structure is what I care about: bacon should have chew and crisp in the same bite, and theirs delivers that consistently across locations, which is the hardest thing to pull off at chain scale.”

articles.headline: Selling Burritos Back To Mexico: Chipotle’s Bold Expansion
articles.author: James Wagner
articles.summary: In the homeland of tacos, burritos and quesadillas, a new competitor has entered the market: Chipotle, the Mexican-inspired fast casual chain that is ubiquitous in the United States. “What pride that the first one in Mexico and in Latin America is here,” said Gaby Rodríguez, 44, a lawyer from Monterrey who was the first person in line, in an affluent suburb of that city. The first 100 customers got a free Chipotle tote bag, T-shirt and hat. Many of Chipotle’s first customers in Mexico were people nostalgic to eat it again after having visited or lived in the United States. One couple met through Chipotle in the United States years ago before moving to Mexico.

articles.headline: Taco Bell Was Crushing It — Then Cyclosporiasis Hit
articles.author: Caroline Petrow-Cohen
articles.summary: Taco Bell was sitting solidly in the sweet spot for fast food in troubled times. The Irvine-based chain had developed a menu that was affordable enough for consumers worried about inflation and also fun enough for those looking for more than just hamburgers and pizza. Its sales and stock price were soaring at a time when fast-food outlets are struggling amid inflation and other industry challenges. Then came cyclosporiasis. A massive parasitic outbreak has taken Taco Bell down a peg, and now it has to rebuild its momentum. “The brand has seen a meaningful near-term sales impact,” said Chris Turner, chief executive of Taco Bell’s owner Yum Brands, on an earnings call Thursday.

articles.headline: DoorDash's CEO Worried A Taco Bell Partnership Wouldn't Work. Instead, It Revealed A Truth About Food Delivery
articles.author: Alex Bitter
articles.summary: DoorDash CEO Tony Xu never expected that people would pay as much as they do for food delivery. The delivery service became one of the biggest companies in tech by delivering food, groceries, and other purchases to customers' homes for a premium over in-store ordering. And people continue to spend on food delivery, even as some cut back on groceries and other essentials. People's willingness to pay extra for the convenience of delivery has surprised even Xu himself, he told the Uncapped with Jack Altman podcast in an episode published on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Yum Bids Pizza Hut Farewell, Overhauls KFC
articles.author: Aneurin Canham-Clyne
articles.summary: Yum Brands closed out Q2 with fundamental strategic shifts at KFC and Pizza Hut, according to the company’s earnings release. In addition to Yum’s decision to sell Pizza Hut for $2.7 billion in two separate transactions, the company debuted a new global brand identity for KFC, which it plans to roll out across its top 20 markets in a “coordinated global effort,” CEO Chris Turner said on a Thursday earnings call. KFC’s international units have long outperformed its U.S. system, and Pizza Hut, before the sale, was the sick man of Yum’s portfolio.

articles.headline: Burger King's Viral Pregnancy Test Stunt Was A Bold Move, But It Worked
articles.author: Joe Foley
articles.summary: Burger King has a difficult relationship with parenthood. Less than a year ago, it ran a campaign showing babies gazing longingly at junk food their parents were eating. Some thought that a tad misguided at a time when childhood obesity is a major health concern. It was worrying, then, when a Burger King Instagram account last week posted a photo of a positive pregnancy test. I mean, is this a brand that's fit to raise a child? Would it be caught trying to wean its offspring on Whoppers? While rival brands fought over who was the father, confusion reigned for a good 24 hours until the meaning of the post became clear.

articles.headline: From KFC To Cane's — Why Chicken Chains Have Taken Over America's Favorite Fast Food
articles.author: Lindsey Reynolds
articles.summary: For decades, burgers have dominated the fast food landscape. We are a country that loves our Big Macs, our smash burgers, and our Double-Doubles. But recently, chicken has been stealing the spotlight. But not every chicken chain is thriving equally. The longtime legacy brand KFC continues to take hits for inconsistent quality, with online commenters posting opinions like: "KFC's quality has really gone downhill in recent years." Then there are zingers such as: "KFC and some other chains have forgotten that not 100% of their customer base are tasteless drones just looking for another serving of slop." These comments are only more proof that newer chicken concepts will continue to thrive.

articles.headline: The 2026 Margin Rebuild: QSR, Retail Franchises And The 'Virtual Shift Lead'
articles.author: Robert Messer
articles.summary: ​The quick service restaurant (QSR) and retail sectors are currently facing a perfect storm. Driven by chronic labor shortages, unpredictable supply chain disruptions and rising wages, operators are feeling an unprecedented squeeze. Food and labor costs have both surged by roughly 35% over the last five years. As a result, the average restaurant profit margin now hovers between a precarious 3% and 5%, and industry data suggests that up to 42% of restaurants are currently struggling just to stay in the black. To protect hardware investments, it is crucial that these cloud-based AI systems remain vendor-agnostic, capable of integrating with leading camera brands already installed in the field. The goal is to streamline the QSR and retail technology stack, not complicate it.

articles.headline: How AI-Powered Digital Signage Drives QSR Growth In 2026
articles.author: Misty Chalk
articles.summary: At the surface, 2026 appears to remain a relatively uncertain year for quick-serve restaurants (QSRs) nationwide. Sources indicate growth percentages in both franchise volume and output are expected to be around 1.6%. The great news, though, is that despite these hurdles, there's still plenty of opportunity for franchises seeking growth to turn the tide. According to an industry report, eight out of 10 operators believe the use of technology improves their competitive advantage. The hardware that powers digital signage has evolved to usher in the new AI era. Franchises can now adopt media players with integrated neural processing units (NPUs), allowing them to transform their operational workflows. This grants the ability to run AI models that unlock new functionality and measurement.

articles.headline: An Increasingly Digitized Fast-Food Industry Looks To Improve Hospitality
articles.author: Jonathan Maze
articles.summary: In a recently remodeled McDonald’s location in Chicago, a set of temperature-controlled cubbies, accessible only by keypad, is stationed next to the door, so delivery drivers can get their orders without walking inside. The restaurant itself features kiosks, like the bulk of the chain’s restaurants. The front counter, in fact, is quite small, with room for just one order taker, if there is one. But there were plenty of workers in the dining room, which was busy on a weekday lunch rush. The employees delivered orders, asked customers if they needed anything and guided folks through the complexities of the kiosk. A group of dine-in customers, including two from McDonald’s corporate, were visited no fewer than four times by employees, who regularly tried engaging in conversation.

articles.headline: Raising Cane's To Open 7 New Restaurants. See Locations
articles.author: Saleen Martin
articles.summary: August marks 30 years of Raising Cane’s Chicken Fingers and this year, the company is welcoming the milestone with seven new store openings and some reopenings. The company plans to open seven new restaurants, including two new markets in eastern North Carolina and southeastern Georgia. There are also plans to reopen four remodeled locations as well, according to a statement the chain sent to USA TODAY. The restaurant said it is focusing on growth.

articles.headline: Papa Murphy's Shutters Up To 50 Stores As U.S. Pizza Industry Slumps
articles.summary: Papa Murphy's, the largest take-and-bake pizza chain in the U.S., is shuttering the bulk of a 68-store closure plan unveiled by parent company MTY Food Group, as the broader pizza industry grapples with falling demand, rising costs, and shifting consumer habits. Of the 68 underperforming corporate-owned locations MTY is closing across its portfolio, up to 50 are Papa Murphy's restaurants, with the remainder spread across the Canadian franchisor's other chains. The closures, announced during MTY Food Group's second-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings call, will begin as early as next week and unfold over the next six to nine months. MTY Food Group CEO Eric Lefebvre said the decision followed a detailed, store-by-store review of the chain's corporate-owned portfolio.

articles.headline: How Coffee Drive Thrus Can Use Tech Without Losing Hospitality
articles.summary: In coffee drive thrus, technology is increasingly positioned as the answer to speed, accuracy, labor pressure, and tighter margins. But guests do not necessarily want a fully automated experience. According to the National Restaurant Association, 62 percent of limited-service guests prefer traditional employee-provided service over an experience involving technology. At the same time, 40 percent said they welcome technology that makes ordering easier and faster. For coffee operators, there should not be a choice between tech and hospitality. Using technology to make hospitality easier to deliver is where the real opportunity lies.

articles.headline: Students Compete To Revolutionize Restaurant Industry In 48 Hours
articles.author: Jhett Sherry
articles.summary: Students from 4 states are facing to see which team can improve fast food dining in just 2 days. Make48’s competition returns to UW-Stout for 3rd time and sees nine middle and high school teams build a prototype and create marketing for their innovation on fast food dining. These teams come from Wisconsin, Minnesota, Missouri and Indiana. To tackle this year’s challenge, teams brainstormed how to improve different parts of the fast-food experience like packaging, cleanliness, and the drive-thru.

articles.headline: Jersey Mike’s Raises $1 Billion, but Shares Fall In Public Debut
articles.summary: Jersey Mike’s joined the public market Thursday in one of the industry’s largest IPOs ever, but its stock finished the day below its offering price. The sandwich chain priced approximately 43.5 million shares at $23 apiece, the midpoint of its marketed range of $21 to $25. The offering raised about $1 billion and gave Jersey Mike’s an initial valuation of roughly $7.3 billion.

articles.headline: The Real Reasons Kentucky Fried Chicken Became KFC
articles.author: Dave Spencer
articles.summary: Before it became official, I wasn't the only one referring to Kentucky Fried Chicken as KFC. Long before the company adopted the acronym in 1991, most of us were already using it. While the 1980s gave us the fitness craze, complete with million-selling home workout videos by Richard Simmons and Jane Fonda, Jazzercise, aerobics, and more, the 1990s were when corporate health consciousness really began influencing our diets. Part of that shift was the Kentucky Fried Chicken name change in 1991, as the company was anxious to downplay the "fried" component of their star attraction in the wake of this shift toward healthier eating. But KFC's trademark cooking method wasn't the only reason for the update; removing the word itself from the brand name allowed the chain to expand its menu into grilled items or, perhaps, even non-chicken items. KFC did, after all, offer ribs on its menu in the late 70s into the early 80s, but that was before the name was changed.

articles.headline: Internet Reacts To Bizarre KFC And Oreo Collab
articles.author: Jalyn Smoot
articles.summary: Courtesy of KFC and Oreo, a new dessert concoction has hit supermarket shelves. Over the years, Oreo has introduced several wild flavors that stray away from its beloved original cookie sandwich, including Fruit Punch, Pumpkin Spice, Waffles and Syrup, Limeade, Candy Cane, and Mint. Oreo has practically sandwiched every known flavor between its two cookies, but its newest innovation may be the craziest one yet. The unexpected cookie crossover debuted in China on July 31 as part of Oreo's limited-edition "Playful Time Travel" collection, according to China Insider. Oddly enough, this isn't KFC's first international endeavor with Oreo. In April 2025, popular food blogger Snackolator shared an image of a "Kentucky Fried Oreo," a menu item that is only available in South Africa.

articles.headline: Taco Bell Met With Michigan On Parasite Weeks Before Recall
articles.author: Daniela Sirtori
articles.summary: Michigan health authorities were in touch with Taco Bell’s parent company, Yum! Brands Inc., about a parasitic outbreak in early July, weeks before the company officially alerted consumers. The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services held a call with Yum on July 2 to discuss cyclospora, according to documents obtained by Bloomberg News through a public records request. In a follow-up email, officials asked to connect with the company’s supply chain quality assurance and communications teams “for a discussion about any intervention or notification that could be taken this week to aid in reducing the number of cases in the future.”

articles.headline: Taco Bell Quietly Brought Back 5 Fan-Favorite Menu Items For A Limited Time
articles.author: Bailey Fink
articles.summary: Most of us know just how serious fast-food fans can be about their favorite restaurants and menu items. The hype surrounding a beloved menu item—especially one that’s been discontinued—can be so strong that if you check the comments on any social media post, you’ll almost always find a few fans asking the chain to bring back x, y, or z. Taco Bell is no stranger to the highs and lows of a devoted fandom. Because the chain is practically always testing and releasing new items, it’s rather typical to see a fan-favorite food or drink axed to make room for something new. However, always the crowd pleaser, Taco Bell continues to reward its fans’ dedication by bringing back discontinued items every so often.

articles.headline: John Oliver Says Trump Administration Has Lost ‘Moral High Ground’ To Taco Bell Amid Explosive Diarrhea Crisis
articles.author: Shania Russell
articles.summary: If you ask John Oliver, the Trump administration should start taking cues from Taco Bell. At least where one issue is concerned. During his Aug. 2 episode, the Last Week Tonight host addressed the horrifying case of “debilitating explosive diarrhea” that’s been sweeping the nation — and hilariously compared the government’s response to that of a certain fast food chain. News of the outbreak first broke last month, when federal health officials identified lettuce served at various Taco Bell locations across five U.S. states as a source of cyclosporiasis, a foodborne illness that can cause weeks of severe diarrhea. In response, the company put out a statement to reassure customers. “We want you to hear it from us. We take your health and safety seriously and have removed all affected Taylor Farms lettuce from Taco Bell stores,” the statement read. “So go ahead and enjoy your Taco Bell today. You always got us. We always got you. See you in the drive-through.”

articles.headline: Wendy’s Brings Back The Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger On Pub-Themed Fall Menu (Plus A New Frosty!)
articles.author: Chiara Kim
articles.summary: Wendy’s is launching pub-themed menu items and a new Frosty in time for fall! The fast food chain announced on Monday, Aug. 3, that it is bringing back the Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger, along with releasing several other pub menu items and an Apple Crumble Frosty Fusion for its fall menu, per a release shared with PEOPLE. Along with the Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger returning to U.S. locations this fall, the new Pretzel Bacon Pub Chicken Sandwich, Bacon Pub Fries and Apple Crumble Frosty Fusion join the chain’s fall lineup, starting on Aug. 3. The Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger features a quarter-pound beef patty, beer cheese sauce, Applewood-smoked bacon, smoky honey mustard, crispy onions, pickles and Muenster cheese on a pretzel bun.

articles.headline: Crisp Days Meet Cozy Bites: Wendy's Brings Pub-Worthy Fall Flavor With New And Returning Seasonal Favorites
articles.summary: Wendy's is bringing back the fan-favorite Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger after consumers voted for its return in the 'Bring it Back' bracket earlier this year. Beginning today, the beloved sandwich returns to restaurants nationwide alongside two Pretzel Bacon Pub menu items and the all-new Apple Crumble Frosty Fusion®, giving Wendy's customers even more reasons to savor the flavors of fall. "The 'Bring It Back' bracket made one thing clear: Wendy's fans wanted the Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger back, and we're excited to deliver," said Lindsay Radkoski, Chief Marketing Officer at Wendy's. "From the Pretzel Bacon Pub lineup to the Apple Crumble Frosty Fusion, this season's menu is packed with the bold, elevated flavors fans are craving. It's the kind of menu inspiration you'd expect to find at your favorite neighborhood pub, now at Wendy's."

articles.headline: The Major Difference Between Burger King And Wendy's Beef
articles.author: Deepak Narayanan
articles.summary: A lot of time, effort, and advertising dollars have gone into fueling America's burger wars since the 1980s. While McDonald's pulled clear early on, Burger King and Wendy's have spent decades jostling for second place. By the mid-'80s, BK doubled down on its size-does-matter approach and the evergreen "Make It a Whopper" campaign, while Wendy's made waves with the iconic "Where's The Beef?" advert. They've since traded blows over several things — revenues, locations, sly jibes, witty comebacks — but at the heart of the difference between these burger giants is what's at the literal center of their businesses: the beef patty. We're not talking about seasoning or cooking times. The major difference between the beef at Burger King and Wendy's is that while BK uses frozen patties, Wendy's only uses fresh beef. Now, it's important to clarify at the outset that fresh or frozen patties cannot directly be linked to quality. Food retains more nutrients when flash-frozen, as it decays slowly.

articles.headline: Wendy’s Brings Back Its Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger
articles.summary: Wendy’s is going back to the pub. The fast-food chain has officially brought back its Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger, along with a chicken sandwich version of a product that won a customer vote during the March Madness NCAA basketball tournaments earlier this year. The company is also introducing an Apple Crumble Frosty Fusion, the latest extension of the chain’s popular line of Frosty desserts. The fusion includes a Vanilla Frosty with spiced apple syrup and oat crumbles. Wendy’s used a social media “bracket” vote to see which product customers wanted to bring back. Four months later, the pub burger is back on the company’s menu.

articles.headline: Chipotle Eyes Takeover Of Old Kettering Wendy’s
articles.author: Carlos Mathis
articles.summary: Just days after a local Wendy’s closed its doors for good, another restaurant chain appears to be interested in the site. WDTN.com obtained documents on Monday, Aug. 3 showing Chipotle’s interest in creating a location at 4003 Wilmington Pike in Kettering. The Wendy’s restaurant abruptly closed in July, with the chain referring customers to its Dorothy Lane location. The applicant wants to conduct interior and exterior renovations to the former Wendy’s building, and convert it to a Chipotle restaurant with a drive-thru pick-up lane. A few days after the location permanently closed, 2 NEWS saw crews at the vacant restaurant removing exterior Wendy’s signage on the building. Currently, the nearest Chipotle to the location is approximately two miles away at The Greene.

articles.headline: HTeaO Launches New Pineapple Chipotle Refresher
articles.summary: HTeaO, the nation’s leading iced tea franchise, is turning up the flavor with the launch of its new Pineapple Chipotle Refresher, featuring Tajín Clásico Seasoning, available for a limited time from August 4 through October 6 at locations nationwide. Made with sweet pineapple, lemonade, a hint of chipotle and a sprinkle of Tajín Clásico Seasoning, the new Pineapple Chipotle Refresher is finished with HTeaO’s signature CleanBoost Energy for a refreshing beverage that delivers the perfect balance of sweet, citrusy and smoky heat. “The Pineapple Chipotle Refresher is one of our most adventurous beverages yet,” said Kelsey McManemin, Senior Vice President of Marketing at HTeaO. “We’ve seen guests embrace bold, globally inspired flavors, and this drink delivers the perfect combination of sweet, smoky and tangy with just the right amount of heat. It’s refreshing, unexpected and exactly the kind of limited-time offering our guests love to discover.”

articles.headline: Burger King On Astoria Boulevard Forced To Temporary Close Due To Numerous Sanitary Violations
articles.author: Shane O’Brien
articles.summary: The city’s Health Department has temporarily shuttered Burger King’s Astoria Boulevard location after observing a number of sanitary violations during an inspection at the restaurant last month. The NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene conducted an inspection at the restaurant at 33-10 Astoria Blvd. on July 29, issuing 49 violation points for issues such as evidence of filth flies or other pests found in the establishment’s food or non-food areas. The Health Department further observed issues such as a lack of an adequate hand-washing facility in a toilet within 25 feet of food preparation areas. The inspection also found that Burger King “is not free of harborage or conditions” conducive to rodents, insects or other pests as well as observing that non-food contact surfaces or equipment were not kept clean.

articles.headline: The 2026 QSR 50: Fast Food’s Leading Annual Report
articles.summary: The brands leading this year’s QSR 50 are succeeding in an environment with cautious consumers, fierce competition, and shifting expectations. Traffic has become harder to earn. Value has become a permanent strategic pillar rather than a temporary promotion. Technology has evolved from a support function into a primary growth driver. And restaurants are being judged not just by how many locations they open, but by how effectively they create reasons for customers to return. Across the ranking, common themes emerge. Artificial intelligence is moving from experimentation to implementation. Loyalty programs are becoming more sophisticated. Beverage innovation is creating new occasions and higher check averages. Also, many legacy brands are reevaluating portfolios, simplifying operations, and searching for more sustainable paths to profitability.

articles.headline: In Sodexo’s Kitchens, AI Is Evolving Into A Valued Sous Chef
articles.author: Patricia Cobe
articles.summary: Sodexo runs foodservice operations at about 27,000 locations around the world, ranging from health care to college dining, schools, and workplaces. “We have over 70,000 recipes in North America alone that support our diverse menu needs,” said Richard Arakelian, VP of culinary and service development for Sodexo North America. “We have team members that are moving from different business segments, and quality, consistency, continuity, and execution are critical. We’re utilizing AI agents now to help with that consistency and continuity and support all our brands from ideation to the central development process.” Arakelian noted that it’s critical these days to get to market quicker and AI helps accelerate systems, menus, photography and a host of other tasks. “We are utilizing AI almost like a sous chef or chef’s companion,” he said. “It helps us develop the culinary brief document we use going into R&D, bringing us on a journey much more rapidly than we had before. AI condenses the development timelines by 50% to 60%.”

articles.headline: DQ’s Kicking Off Fall Flavor Season With These New Treats
articles.author: Mark Heim
articles.summary: Dairy Queen is rolling out its fall cravings starting this month. The new Caramel Apple Cheesecake BLIZZARD® Treat is August’s Blizzard of the Month, featuring cheesecake pieces and caramel apple topping blended with world famous DQ soft serve to Blizzard perfection. What better is there to get in the spirit of fall while dealing with the summer heat. DQ is also giving fans something to “flip” for this month with its Double Flip digital offer. Available though Aug. 30 in the DQ App, DQ reward members can buy one Blizzard Treat and get a second for just 99 cents, which, of course, is a nod to the iconic upside-down flip that has made the classic treats famous.

articles.headline: Popeyes Latest Value Deal Features Its New Tenders
articles.author: Alicia Kelso
articles.summary: Popeyes’ upgraded chicken tenders are back in the spotlight as part of a new $9.99 Tenders Deal available now through Aug. 30. The meal includes four hand-battered and breaded tenders — available in classic, spicy or blackened — a regular side, regular drink, and signature buttermilk biscuit for $9.99. Popeyes joins a growing number of restaurant chains upgrading their chicken offerings as the category intensifies and consumers continue to pull back on visits. Chili’s, BJ’s Restaurants, and Culver’s all recently upgraded their chicken sandwich offerings, for example, while McDonald’s is testing larger, crispier McCrispy Strips.

articles.headline: Chick-Fil-A Confirms Visalia Restaurant Is Still On Track For 2027
articles.author: Steve Pastis
articles.summary: Yes, Chick-fil-A is still coming to Visalia, even though the process may seem to be moving slowly. “It’s our pleasure to confirm we will be opening our first Chick-fil-A restaurant in Visalia in 2027,” said Chick-fil-A in a statement. “We look forward to joining the community and serving all of our guests delicious food in an environment of genuine hospitality and care.” Chick-fil-A said each of its restaurant creates 80 to 120 jobs. Plans call for a 5,053-square-foot restaurant, which will include seating for 92 and feature a two-lane drive-through, to be built at the corner of Mooney Boulevard and Visalia Parkway.

articles.headline: Raising Cane’s To Open Several New Locations In August, With Even More On The Way
articles.author: Addy Bink
articles.summary: It’s been 30 years since Caniacs had their first chance at enjoying their chicken fingers with Cane’s Sauce and a side of Texas toast. Now, the fast food chicken chain Raising Cane’s is looking to bring its largely unchanged menu to even more locations. The first Raising Cane’s opened its doors in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, in 1996. Since then, Cane’s has grown to have more than 950 locations across 44 states, the District of Columbia, and Guam. An additional seven locations are on track to open in August, with even more in the works. Cane’s is also reopening four recently remodeled locations this month. The first, reopening on August 12, is on Texas Avenue in College Station, Texas. Days later, on August 17, locations on Las Vegas Boulevard in Las Vegas and Nicholasville Road in Lexington, Kentucky, will reopen. The final Cane’s location, on Hamilton Road in Gahanna, Ohio, reopens on August 24.

articles.headline: Meant To Compete With KFC, This Classic 1960s Chain Collapsed After Just A Few Years
articles.author: Brandon Rich
articles.summary: America isn't short on fried chicken fast food chains. Yet, when you stop to think about the type that exist out there, it can feel like a carefully crafted ecosystem. Sure, competition exists, but anyone hunting for fried chicken might feel that each chain is unique in its own way. Popeyes isn't Chick-fil-A, and Zaxby's is distinct from Raising Cane's. To that end, it's hard to imagine a chain giving KFC a run for its money in a category of food that it basically invented. Yet back in the 1960s, that's exactly what one classic chicken chain tried to do. The company was known as Minnie Pearl's Fried Chicken (legally, Minnie Pearl's Chicken System Inc.), and it lasted shorter than a bubble of oil in a fryer — metaphorically, of course.

articles.headline: KFC Founder Puts Up Personal Cookery Collection For Sale
articles.author: Owen Gough
articles.summary: KFC founder Colonel Sanders’ signature black bow tie, cookery equipment, personal planner and dozens of other special items generated close to US$300,000 (£260,000) at auction last week. The KFC founder, who died in 1980, was the well-known face of the global brand, originally known as Kentucky Fried Chicken. Sanders’ clip-on black ribbon bow tie, which he is famously seen wearing in the fried chicken giant’s logo, sold for $8,000 (£6,900). His former home and another restaurant he owned were also up for auction as well as the 100 or so artefacts sold last week. Sanders’ personal 1964 planner, featuring a handwritten list of herbs and spices that was the subject of an early 2000s lawsuit filed by the KFC Corp, brought in the largest amount of the night, selling for $30,000 (£26,000).

articles.headline: Taco Bell Diners Vow Never To Eat Beans Again After Worker Exposes How Beans Are Made: ‘Disgusting’
articles.author: Asia Grace
articles.summary: They’re spilling the beans on The Bell — and it’s giving some grubbers nauseating hell. Fast foodies are sourly split as a trending vid allegedly reveals the “disgusting” manner in which Taco Bell prepares its beans. And while queasy critics call for the health inspector, unfazed fans are championing the chow with a “chef’s kiss” stamp of approval. It’s the hottest beans beef of 2026. Visuals of the controversial food prep, shared via @ItzSleepyPanz, features a kitchen employee dumping warm water atop brown, dehydrated, stringy scraps, allegedly stirring the blend into Taco Bell’s refried delights. The eye-popping post has amassed over 13 million views from divided digital audiences worldwide.

articles.headline: First It Was Taco Bell. Now Chipotle Is At The Center Of A Foodborne Outbreak
articles.author: Krystal Nurse
articles.summary: Frustrated about having to avoid lettuce and Taco Bell in fear of contracting cyclosporiasis? It may be time to add Chipotle’s jalapeños to that list after Minnesota public health officials announced they are investigating a salmonella outbreak. At least 110 people in Minnesota have fallen ill with salmonella, Reuters reported, with 75 telling the Minnesota Department of Health they ate at Chipotle between June 14 and July 14. Chipotle said in a Tuesday statement that it conducted an internal investigation and found its jalapeños to be the culprit. “As part of our established health and safety protocols, upon learning of a potential outbreak, we immediately initiated our ingredient traceability system and were able to identify jalapeños as a potential common ingredient from a common lot, and the restaurants where it was distributed,” the restaurant said.

articles.headline: Wendy’s Brings Back Beloved Burger After Fan Vote, Reveals New Seasonal Frosty
articles.author: Brandon Champion
articles.summary: Wendy’s is bringing back a favorite burger and revealed a seasonal Frosty flavor perfect for fall. The fast-food chain made several announcements this week, most notably that its fan-favorite Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger will return to menus nationwide after customers voted for its return in the 'Bring it Back' bracket earlier this year. The burger features a quarter-pound beef patty, beer cheese sauce, Applewood-smoked bacon, smoky honey mustard, crispy onions, pickles and a slice of Muenster Cheese all on a soft, pretzel bun.

articles.headline: Plan For New Wendy's Revealed
articles.author: David L. Dye
articles.summary: The City of Hermitage’s only Wendy’s restaurant will eventually be moved to a new spot within walking distance of its current location. The major land development plan for a new Wendy’s was unanimously approved by the Hermitage Planning Commission during the commission’s monthly meeting Monday morning.

articles.headline: Chipotle Removes Jalapeños Linked To Salmonella Outbreak From Its Restaurants
articles.author: Alena Cerro
articles.summary: A salmonella outbreak that has sickened dozens of people in Minnesota prompted Chipotle Mexican Grill to announce on Tuesday that it was pulling certain jalapeños from its restaurants. In a statement, the company said “Chipotle has removed the suspect jalapeños across all of our restaurants where they had been distributed and replaced them with jalapeños from different growers.” It was unclear how many restaurants were affected and in which states. Laurie Schalow, the chief corporate affairs and food safety officer for Chipotle, highlighted the company’s “robust ingredient traceability system,” and said in the statement that it had “proactively identified jalapeños as a potential common ingredient from a common lot.”

articles.headline: What's The Actual Difference Between Burger King And McDonald's Beef?
articles.author: Lindsey Reynolds
articles.summary: Unless you're a hardcore fan, the beef served at McDonald's and Burger King seems pretty similar. Both chains advertise burgers made from 100% beef, both avoid fillers and extenders in their patties, and both have spent millions advertising that their burgers contain nothing more than beef and seasoning. However, if you're willing to dig into how each company prepares and serves its burgers, some noticeable differences do emerge. Burger King does things a little differently. The chain has used frozen patties since its opening in 1954. What Burger King tries to emphasize instead is its signature cooking style: The famous flame-grilling method. Because BK cooks with a proprietary commercial broiler, that distinctive chargrilled flavor really comes through, especially on its best-selling Whopper. Meanwhile, McDonald's sticks to a flat-top grill, which cooks multiple patties in their own juices extremely quickly. Neither burger is better, per se, but different cooking methods certainly yield different flavor profiles.

articles.headline: Business World Stunned That a Restaurant Chain Is Doing Well Without Mindlessly Embracing AI
articles.author: Frank Landymore
articles.summary: Not immediately jumping on the AI bandwagon like everyone else is? It says something that Chili’s doing this— yes, the casual dining chain with the big red pepper logo — is being seen as shrewd decision making and not just common sense. Chris Caldwell, the chief information officer at Chili’s owner Brinker International, emphasized in recent interviews how the company wasn’t “all in” on AI, and is instead focused on overhauling its tech in more practical ways. “I’m not chasing AI to go, ‘Guys, Anthropic just released a new LLM, and we need to use it because it’s cool,'” he told Business Insider.

articles.headline: The Brown Bag AI Lunches Are Over
articles.author: Lila MacLellan
articles.summary: By now most people have discovered the joy of asking AI highly specific logistical questions. What’s the best route to drive from Detroit to New York this weekend dodging thunderstorms and without losing cell service? Or, as Debby Soo, CEO of OpenTable, recently suggested of a typical ChatGPT restaurant search: “I’m looking for a seafood restaurant that’s celiac-friendly, but has been nominated for a James Beard, in Boston, this Friday at seven.” Today, Soo needs to not only meet consumers and restaurants wherever they are—and restaurant goers are using AI searches more and more, she said—but also compete against a slew of rivals, like Yelp and Resy, in what has become a cutthroat space. That requires putting AI behind everything, of course—while increasingly holding employees accountable for learning how to use it.

articles.headline: McDonald’s Struggles To Attract Bargain-Hungry Customers
articles.author: Rob Wile
articles.summary: Having trouble figuring out this economy? So is McDonald’s. The fast-food giant reported its slowest U.S. sales growth in over a year as its value push fell flat with customers who continue to struggle with higher prices. Overall U.S. customer count declined. Company executives said it provided too many value offers, including a $3-and-under menu and $5 bundled meal deals, that ended up muddling the chain’s message to people who are as hungry for bargains as they are for convenient food. “We simply didn’t execute at the level we needed to in the second quarter,” CEO Chris Kempczinski said in a statement Tuesday. The company must “raise the bar in the U.S. and accelerate performance in our largest market.”

articles.headline: McDonald’s Aims To Improve Service And Food, And Chose A New U.S. Boss To Help
articles.author: Heather Haddon
articles.summary: McDonald’s is shaking up its U.S. business, picking a new leader to help boost sluggish domestic sales and improve service and quality at the world’s biggest burger chain. The company on Tuesday appointed Skye Anderson president of its U.S. business, succeeding Joe Erlinger, who had held the role since 2019. It marked a rapid advance for Anderson, a 26-year veteran of the company who was named U.S. chief operating officer in April after serving in a global business role.

articles.headline: A Fast-Food Chicken Chain Is Opening Its Second Oregon Restaurant This Fall. More Might Be On The Way
articles.author: Veronica Nocera
articles.summary: There can never be too much fast-food fried chicken. Raising Cane’s is making sure of that. The Baton Rouge-based chain has been working to expand its footprint in the Willamette Valley and beyond, bringing its fan-favorite chicken fingers and sauce to new audiences. One of those restaurants, located just outside Portland, will open its doors this fall.

articles.headline: Springfield To Get A Second Chick-Fil-A Restaurant
articles.author: Patricia Cobe
articles.summary: After months of rumors, one of the most popular fast-food chicken restaurants in the country will be adding a second location in the capital city. On July 31, a commercial building permit was issued by the City of Springfield Building and Zoning Department to Chick-fil-A for the construction of a new fast-food restaurant with a drive thru, parking lot and associated utilities.

articles.headline: Bankrupt Fried Chicken Chain Franchisee Is Closing 39 Restaurants After Selling Off The Rest
articles.author: Tamilore Onikosi
articles.summary: Georgia and Florida residents who love their Popeyes fried chicken would be sad to know that they have 39 fewer locations to choose from as of July 2026. The closures — 31 in Florida and eight in Georgia — followed the collapse of Sailormen Inc., a major Popeyes franchisee that operated restaurants across both states. After filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in January 2026, Sailormen attempted to sell as much of its restaurant portfolio as possible, but ultimately shut down the locations for which it could not secure buyers.

articles.headline: Salmonella Outbreak Linked To Jalapeños Expands To 27 States
articles.author: Berkeley Lovelace Jr. and Lauren Dunn
articles.summary: Federal health officials are investigating a salmonella outbreak tied to jalapeños that has sickened 345 people in 27 states, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said Wednesday. The jalapeños were supplied by California-based Coast Citrus Distributors and sourced from Mexico, the CDC said. They were served at Chipotle, Qdoba and other restaurants. Chipotle said Tuesday that it had removed jalapeños from its menu “out of an abundance of caution.” On Wednesday, Qdoba said it had “proactively removed jalapeños from all our restaurants.”

articles.headline: Chipotle Says Annual Targets Do Not Include Impact Of Minnesota Salmonella Outbreak
articles.author: Juveria Tabassum
articles.summary: Chipotle Mexican Grill said on Wednesday its annual targets shared last week did not include the financial impact from the salmonella ​outbreak in Minnesota, which resulted in the burrito chain ‌pulling jalepenos at some of its restaurants. The Minnesota Department of Health said on Tuesday it had identified 110 salmonella outbreak-related cases in the ​state, with 75 of 84 people interviewed reporting eating at ​Chipotle between June 14 and July 14. Also on Tuesday, ⁠Chipotle said it had begun tracing ingredients through its supply chain ​after learning of the potential salmonella outbreak.

articles.headline: Wendy’s Store Closures 2026: Fast-Food Chain Update On Long List Of Locations Shuttered In Turnaround Plan
articles.author: Jennifer Mattson
articles.summary: Wendy’s shares rose on Friday after the fast-food giant reported stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings, beating analyst estimates despite poor U.S. store performance, with U.S. same-restaurant sales falling 7.8%. That slow but steady growth reflects the burger chain’s effort to turn around sales by shedding low-performing American restaurants and improving menu quality. The plan comes amid an overall decline in fast-food store traffic, as American consumers grapple with higher prices and the cost of food and living soars. “We are in the early innings of our turnaround,” Ken Cook, Wendy’s CFO and interim CEO, told analysts on Friday’s earnings call.

articles.headline: Everything You Need To Know About KFC’s New Ted Lasso Deal
articles.author: Jay Wilson
articles.summary: Ted Lasso is coming back. In fact, Ted Lasso IS back. The first episode of the fourth season of this blockbuster show drops today on Apple TV, and you may well have heard about it. The build-up to Ted Lasso’s apparent last season (after LAST season was meant to be its last season, but there was more story to tell, people!) has been punctuated not just by press appointments with the cast, but with food tie-ins. A few weeks ago, Jeni’s ice cream released a Ted Lasso flavor – and now, KFC’s getting involved, with a deal of its own. In honor of the underdog feel that permeates the show, and the comeback both of AFC Richmond and of the series itself, KFC is releasing its “Comeback Bucket.”

articles.headline: This Chicken Item Is The Worst Side On Burger King's Permanent Menu
articles.author: Autumn Swiers
articles.summary: Hitting the drive-thru? Our ultimate Burger King ordering hack is "skip the chicken fries." In Tasting Table's ranking of eight Burger King sides, the chicken fries landed in sixth place, making them the lowest-rated option on the chain's permanent menu. The crispy tacos and cheddar ranch tots ranked even lower, but luckily, these back-of-the-pack sides are available for a limited time only. As for BK's disappointing chicken fries, we're scratching our heads as to why they landed a tenure spot. The appeal of Burger King's chicken fries relies heavily on novelty. Breaded chicken strips shaped like French fries offer a playful concept. They're also easily dippable — and, indeed, a generous dunk in sauce is pretty much the only way to make these dried-out sticks palatable, according to our taste-test.

articles.headline: Taco Bell Knew About Parasite Weeks Before Formal Action: Report
articles.author: Anna Schier
articles.summary: Health officials in Michigan were in contact with Taco Bell’s parent company about the sweeping Cyclospora outbreak that sickened thousands weeks before the company formally alerted consumers, according to a Bloomberg story published this week by multiple news outlets. Parasitic illness cases in 15 states have been linked to iceberg lettuce, U.S. health authorities said Wednesday. Investigators initially narrowed in on lettuce served at Taco Bell, with federal officials subsequently saying they were focused on Taylor Farms as the source of the lettuce in the outbreak, with that company recalling iceberg lettuce grown in central Mexico.

articles.headline: Wendy’s Fall Menu Brings Back Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger
articles.author: Michael Carpenter
articles.summary: Wendy’s is bringing back the Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger starting August 3, 2026, after fans voted for its return in the chain’s Bring it Back bracket earlier this year. The returning sandwich is joined by two new Pretzel Bacon Pub additions and the all-new Apple Crumble Frosty Fusion, rounding out Wendy’s limited-time fall lineup. The Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger features Wendy’s fresh, never-frozen quarter-pound beef patty topped with Beer Cheese Sauce, Applewood-smoked Bacon, Smoky Honey Mustard, Crispy Onions, Pickles, and Muenster Cheese, all on a soft pretzel bun.

articles.headline: Toast Aims To Drive AI Into Dining
articles.author: Justin Bachman
articles.summary: Toast, the restaurant software and payments firm, is working to capture more business from time-strapped customers by using artificial intelligence tools to assume more of a restaurateur’s workflows. Toast’s first AI-enabled workflow product – a digital marketing tool called Toast IQ Grow – is poised to become the company’s fastest-growing product, with executives expecting it to generate $10 million in annual revenue since its May introduction, co-founder and CEO Aman Narang said Tuesday on a quarterly earnings call with analysts. He didn’t specify when the product would reach that sales level. Many Toast customers are unable to leverage the company’s various offerings, and often outsource major functions such as marketing, payroll and bookkeeping, Narang said. Toast believes that AI will allow it to take on more of a restaurant’s work, he said.

articles.headline: The Restaurant Tech Fix That Saves Time, Money, And Headaches
articles.summary: The biggest expense for most restaurants isn't food costs, rent or mortgage costs, or overheads like utilities or insurance. For most restaurants in America, regardless of size, the biggest expense is labor. The better a restaurant can manage labor costs, the more profit the operation stands to generate. And yet restaurant operators frequently bemoan the tech sprawl of separate digital platforms for hiring, scheduling, payroll, inventory, and more. A single scheduling and team management platform, like HotSchedules, can reduce those losses by helping with hiring, shift scheduling, cost forecasting, attendance tracking, and more. All of it is assisted by AI, driven by humans, with the ultimate goals of satisfied customers, engaged employees, and increased profitability.

articles.headline: McDonald’s Journey To 50,000 Restaurants Will Take A Bit Longer
articles.author: Jonathan Maze
articles.summary: McDonald’s over the past three years has embarked on the most ambitious expansion effort in company history, all in a bid to get to 50,000 global locations by 2027. The economy has had a thing or two to say about that, however. The fast-food giant now expects to reach that mark by 2028, executives said this week. That still represents massive expansion. The company finished 2025 with just over 45,000 global restaurants, including 13,706 in the U.S. So that will represent just over 5,000 locations over the next two-plus years.

articles.headline: 27 Restaurant Executives On The Move In July, Including New CEOs At Cracker Barrel And True Food Kitchen
articles.author: Leigh Anne Zinsmeister
articles.summary: It’s shaping up to be a busy month for restaurant C-suites, with 27 executives in the industry taking on new roles last month, including six each in marketing and operations functions. P.F. Chang’s is designing a marketing team focused on social media, including a new director of marketing communications role, which it has now filled via promotion. A fast-casual veteran has moved over to Starbird as it expands. Pollo Campero hired a VP of marketing to focus on U.S. Hispanic consumers. Ziggi’s, Amazing Brands, and Firebirds Wood Fired Grill also have new marketing execs. On the operations side, Fresh Kitchen has added an SVP as well as a development officer; PopUp Bagels appointed a COO; KFC Global has a new COO; and there are also new appointees at Denny’s, Newk’s Eatery, and Uncommon Brands.

articles.headline: QSR Evolution Conference Expands With Debut Of ‘Startup Alley,’ Spotlighting Next-Gen Tech And Culinary Disrupters
articles.summary: The QSR Evolution Conference, the only event of its kind focused exclusively on the needs of quick-service restaurant operators, executives, and leaders, is officially expanding its footprint. Event organizers announced the launch of Startup Alley, a brand-new, dedicated exhibition space designed to highlight the rising stars and disruptive forces reshaping the fast-food and fast-casual landscapes. As the industry faces a rapidly shifting landscape driven by automation, evolving consumer habits, and AI-driven tech, Startup Alley will serve as a launchpad for early stage companies offering groundbreaking solutions in restaurant technology, supply chain efficiency, guest engagement, and culinary innovation.

articles.headline: This Restaurant Is In Higher Demand In The US Than Any Other, Report Says
articles.author: Nicolette Baker
articles.summary: Kebab restaurants have the highest search interest compared to number of restaurants in the United States, outperforming French, Greek, steak house, and diner categories in a new analysis of Google search data. The report suggests Americans are seeking a wider range of cuisines, with Korean, Indian, Chinese, Mexican, and Greek restaurants also ranking among the most searched categories relative to availability. The analysis compared Google search volume with the number of existing restaurants nationwide and in major cities to identify cuisines with the largest gap between consumer search interest and restaurant availability, reflecting search interest rather than actual dining behavior.

articles.headline: America’s Second-Largest Burger Chain Disappeared Forever
articles.author: Paolo Songco
articles.summary: Burger Chef started in Indianapolis in 1958, founded by brothers Donald and Frank Thomas. The chain originally launched to showcase equipment made by their parent company, General Equipment. Its signature flame broiler gave burgers a smoky, grilled taste that stood out from competitors. By 1971, Burger Chef had grown to more than 1,200 locations, trailing only McDonald’s nationwide. General Foods bought the chain in 1968 and pushed further expansion, including into Australia. The international effort ultimately lost significant money for the company.
